/**
 * Dealify plan and entitlement rules. Keep this module pure so both the app
 * server and scanner service can use the same access limits.
 */

export const TRIAL_DAYS = 7
export const SUBSCRIPTION_DAYS = 30
export const PLAN_IDS = ['starter', 'pro'] as const
export type PaidPlanId = (typeof PLAN_IDS)[number]

export const PLAN_CATALOG = {
  starter: {
    label: 'Starter',
    price: 9.99,
    minIntervalSeconds: 600,
    maxWatchlists: 1,
    trackingLine: 'Tracks every 10 minutes',
    features: ['Deal feed with profit scoring', 'Market value estimates'],
  },
  pro: {
    label: 'Pro',
    price: 19.99,
    minIntervalSeconds: 300,
    maxWatchlists: 5,
    trackingLine: 'Tracks every 5 minutes',
    features: [
      'Everything in Starter',
      'Live comparable listings',
      'New-listing and price-drop alerts',
      'Detailed valuations and flip plans',
      'Offer strategy on every deal',
    ],
  },
} as const

export type PlanTier = PaidPlanId | 'locked'

export function isPaidPlan(value: string): value is PaidPlanId {
  return (PLAN_IDS as readonly string[]).includes(value)
}

export function normalizePaidPlan(value: string): PaidPlanId {
  // Existing Plus subscribers map to the new Pro tier (same $19.99 price).
  if (value === 'plus') return 'pro'
  return isPaidPlan(value) ? value : 'pro'
}

export interface PlanUserRow {
  plan: string
  subscriptionStatus: string
  currentPeriodEnd: Date | null
  subscribedAt: Date | null
  canceledAt: Date | null
  trialEndsAt: Date | null
  trialUsedAt: Date | null
}

export interface PlanLimitsView {
  minIntervalMinutes: number
  minIntervalSeconds: number
  maxWatchlists: number
  trackingLine: string
}

export interface PlanState {
  tier: PlanTier
  isTrial: boolean
  trialEndsAt: string | null
  trialMsRemaining: number
  trialAvailable: boolean
  subscriptionStatus: 'none' | 'active' | 'canceled' | 'expired'
  currentPeriodEnd: string | null
  subscribedAt: string | null
  canceledAt: string | null
  proUntil: string | null
  price: number
  limits: PlanLimitsView
}

export function trialMsRemaining(u: PlanUserRow): number {
  if (!u.trialEndsAt) return 0
  return Math.max(0, u.trialEndsAt.getTime() - Date.now())
}

export function paidPeriodMsRemaining(u: PlanUserRow): number {

## Objective - Polish and enhance the Dealify landing page, add the user-provided Dealify logo, remove the "Live across 4 marketplaces" pill, and add a scrolling animation. ## Requirements - Use the attached logo image as the site logo. - Remove the hero pill that says "Live across 4 marketplaces". - Add a scrolling animation to the landing page. - Earlier request: make the landing page look professional and premium. ## Decisions - Launch the app on port 3001 because an existing Dealify server already occupies port 3000 from a different directory. - Use the extracted PNG logo (transparent background, 1352x901 source) rather than recreating it as SVG. - Generate optimized assets: full lockup, mark-only, and square icon. - Interpret "scrolling animation" as both scroll-triggered reveal animations and a subtle marketplace marquee. ## Work State ### Completed - Extracted project to `/Users/fredericvonmengersen/Documents/Default Project/Dealify-project`. - Installed dependencies, created `.env` from the project template, ran `bun run db:push`, started dev server on port 3001. - Landing page polish completed: hero status/stat additions, filled phone feed examples, marketplaces strip, example cards in empty "Current scan" section, pricing/CTA trust rows, icon cards. - Fixed `ListingPhoto` lint issue and missing `phoneDeals` in `src/app/page.tsx` fallback stats. - Extracted the attached logo from OpenCode session DB to `/tmp/dealify-logo.png`; confirmed transparent alpha channel. - Created trimmed logo assets: - `public/logo.png` — 600x159 full lockup - `public/logo-mark.png` — 254x256 mark only - `public/icon.png` — 512x512 square favicon - Logo assets are generated but **not yet wired into components**. ### Active - Replace existing logo/brand marks in landing nav/footer (and likely auth/onboarding headers) with `public/logo.png`. - Remove the "Live across 4 marketplaces" pill from the hero. - Implement scroll-reveal animation in `FadeUp` and a marquee in `MarketStrip`. - Update metadata icons from `/logo.svg` to `/icon.png`. ### Blocked - (none) ## Next Move 1. Update `Logo` in `src/components/landing/landing-page.tsx` to render ``; remove/update `dark` prop usages. 2. Replace brand marks in `src/components/landing/auth-page.tsx` (two instances) and `src/components/landing/onboarding-funnel.tsx` header with the new logo. 3. Delete the hero `

` block containing "Live across 4 marketplaces" in `landing-page.tsx`. 4. Implement `FadeUp` with `useRef` + `IntersectionObserver` scroll-reveal, respecting `prefers-reduced-motion`. 5. Convert `MarketStrip` list to a duplicated, CSS-marquee loop using existing `.animate-marquee`/`.marquee-paused` classes. 6. Update `src/app/layout.tsx` metadata icons to `/icon.png` (type `image/png`) and optionally add `apple` icon. 7. Run `bunx tsc --noEmit` and `bunx eslint src/components/landing/landing-page.tsx src/app/page.tsx`; verify `http://localhost:3001` returns 200. ## Relevant Files - `src/components/landing/landing-page.tsx`: main landing page; `Logo` at ~line 119, hero pill/stat area, `FadeUp`, `MarketStrip`, `LiveHunt`. - `src/app/layout.tsx`: metadata/icons; currently references `/logo.svg`. - `src/components/landing/auth-page.tsx`: brand marks at ~lines 96 and 466 using `Zap` icon. - `src/components/landing/onboarding-funnel.tsx`: brand mark at ~line 295 using `Zap`. - `src/app/globals.css`: `.animate-marquee`, `.marquee-paused`, `.dealify-mark`, landing styles. - `public/logo.png`: new 600x159 full logo lockup. - `public/logo-mark.png`: new 254x256 logo mark. - `public/icon.png`: new 512x512 favicon/app icon. - `/tmp/dealify-logo.png`: original extracted transparent PNG. - `.zscripts/dev-3001.log`: dev server log. ## Important Context - Dev server runs at `http://localhost:3001`; stop with `lsof -ti:3001 | xargs kill`. - TypeScript and ESLint were clean before the current logo/animation work. - `src/app/page.tsx` fallback stats now includes `phoneDeals: []`. - The logo image is white wordmark + orange gradient mark; it works on the dark UI. - The session DB attachment can be re-extracted via `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` table `session_message` where `type='user'` and `data LIKE '%iVBORw0KGgo%'`, field `.files[0].data` (base64). - Scanner mini-service is not running; live listings will not populate until `bun run dev` is run in `mini-services/scanner-service`. - Headless Chrome screenshots require a unique `--user-data-dir`; hash URLs render blank in this setup, so verify sections via tall window screenshots or code review.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Dealify stack watchdog — idempotent, safe to run any time.
#
# Keeps two long-lived services alive (see Task 62 in worklog.md):
#   :3000  Next.js web app   — owned by ONE `bun .zscripts/web-supervisor.ts`,
#                              which respawns `next dev` on every crash
#   :3003  scanner service   — owned by ONE `bun mini-services/scanner-service/
#                              supervisor.ts`, which respawns the scanner
#
# Layering: the in-process supervisors handle crashes within seconds; THIS
# script handles the bigger failures they can't (a supervisor itself dying,
# sandbox recycles that kill everything, duplicate-supervisor pile-ups from
# earlier sessions). It runs from the 10-minute cron watchdog and is safe to
# run manually. On a fresh sandbox it cold-boots the whole stack in ~1 min.
#
# To intentionally take the stack down (e.g. a production build that needs
# port 3000):   touch /tmp/dealify-stack-paused
# and resume:   rm -f /tmp/dealify-stack-paused && bash scripts/ensure-stack.sh

set -u
cd /home/z/my-project

WEB_PORT=3000
SCAN_PORT=3003
WEB_SUP_LOCK=/tmp/dealify-web-supervisor.lock
SCAN_SUP_LOCK=/tmp/dealify-scanner-supervisor.lock

log() { echo "[ensure-stack $(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $*"; }

# ---- predicates -----------------------------------------------------------

# serving <port> — any HTTP answer below 500 means a live server
serving() {
  local code
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 4 -w '%{http_code}' "http://localhost:$1/" 2>/dev/null)
  [ "$code" -ge 100 ] 2>/dev/null && [ "$code" -lt 500 ] 2>/dev/null
}

# ---- /proc helpers ----------------------------------------------------------

cmd_of() { tr '\0' ' ' < "/proc/$1/cmdline" 2>/dev/null; }

# pids whose full cmdline contains the given substring (never self)
pids_matching() {
  local pat="$1" d pid cmd
  for d in /proc/[0-9]*; do
    pid=${d#/proc/}
    [ "$pid" = "$$" ] && continue
    cmd=$(cmd_of "$pid")
    [ -n "$cmd" ] || continue
    case "$cmd" in *"$pat"*) echo "$pid" ;; esac
  done
}

# scanner children: `bun --hot index.ts` whose cwd is the scanner-service dir
# (the cmdline alone is too generic — "index.ts" — so match on cwd)
scanner_child_pids() {
  local d pid cmd cwd
  for d in /proc/[0-9]*; do
    pid=${d#/proc/}
    [ "$pid" = "$$" ] && continue
    cmd=$(cmd_of "$pid")
    case "$cmd" in *index.ts*) ;; *) continue ;; esac
    cwd=$(readlink "$d/cwd" 2>/dev/null) || continue
    [ "$cwd" = "/home/z/my-project/mini-services/scanner-service" ] && echo "$pid"
  done
}

# graceful TERM, 1s, then KILL — for every current match
kill_matching() {
  local pat="$1" p
  for p in $(pids_matching "$pat"); do kill "$p" 2>/dev/null; done
  sleep 1
  for p in $(pids_matching "$pat"); do kill -9 "$p" 2>/dev/null; done
}

kill_scanner_children() {
  local p
  for p in $(scanner_child_pids); do kill "$p" 2>/dev/null; done
  sleep 1
  for p in $(scanner_child_pids); do kill -9 "$p" 2>/dev/null; done
}

# lock_owner_ok <lockfile> <cmdline-substr> — the pid in the lock is alive
# AND running the expected program (guards against recycled pids)
lock_owner_ok() {
  local pid cmd
  pid=$(cat "$1" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  pid=${pid%%[!0-9]*}
  [ -n "$pid" ] || return 1
  cmd=$(cmd_of "$pid")
  case "$cmd" in *"$2"*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
}

wait_serving() { # <port> <timeout-seconds>
  local i
  for ((i = 0; i < $2 * 2; i++)); do
    serving "$1" && return 0
    sleep 0.5
  done
  return 1
}

# ---- gate: intentional pause ------------------------------------------------

if [ -f /tmp/dealify-stack-paused ]; then
  log "paused (/tmp/dealify-stack-paused present) — leaving the stack alone"
  log "STATUS: paused"
  exit 0
fi

# ---- gate: never two cleanups racing (cron tick + manual run) ----------------

exec 9>/tmp/dealify-ensure-stack.flock
if ! flock -n 9; then
  log "another ensure-stack run holds the flock — exiting (it will converge)"
  log "STATUS: concurrent-run-skipped"
  exit 0
fi

No dedicated preferences columns. We can add preferences via localStorage (client-only) for things like appearance/feed density, notification toggles (browser), etc. But "add more in the settings option inside the profile" could simply mean more UI sections/options, some of which are functional with existing endpoints.

Let's inspect `src/lib/api.ts` around profile save and billing/session, plus PushOptIn, and the UI components available (Switch, Select, Tabs, Separator). Also check what app-wide preferences are feasible:
- **Display name**: API has no update endpoint for name. We could add PATCH to `/api/profile` to update name. That's real and useful. Add a "Profile details" section with name input and save.
- **Email**: display only (change email requires verification; too much).
- **Password**: there's forgot-password flow. Could add "Change password" that sends a reset link to email (calls `/api/auth/forgot-password`). Functional. Let's check that route's body.
- **Notifications**: PushOptIn exists. Add notification preference toggles for "New good deals" and "Price drops" — do these actually gate pushes? Let's check push sending code to see if there are prefs. If not, we can add a localStorage-based toggle but it won't affect server pushes. Could be misleading. Better to add only functional toggles.
- **Feed preferences**: e.g., "Hide dismissed deals" might already be feed behavior. "Compact view" could be a localStorage class. But not asked specifically.
- **Scanning**: link to watchlists, show plan cadence, pause all scanning? There's watchlist `active/paused` fields. Could add a "Pause all watchlists" button (functional via existing API). Let's check watchlist API for pause support. It would be a nice settings addition.
- **Currency**: maybe app uses user location currency; no preference.
- **Data**: export data as JSON. Could add an endpoint or client-side fetch from existing APIs (session, watchlists, listings, alerts, profile, billing) and download. Functional and useful.
- **App info**: version, support email, legal links already.
- **Sign out all devices**: server route could delete all AuthSessions except current; not existing. Could add. Maybe overkill.
- **Appearance**: theme is dark-only, so no theme toggle.

Now decide scope. The settings panel currently has: Account, Notifications (push), Legal, Danger zone. "Add more in the settings option inside the profile" likely wants richer settings. We can add:

1. **Profile details** (edit display name) — requires PATCH /api/profile or a new endpoint. Could add PATCH handler to profile route accepting `{ name }`. Then UI with input + save. This is genuinely useful. Also show email with verified badge.

2. **Scanning preferences** — section showing plan cadence (Starter 10 min / Pro 5 min), total watchlists, and a "Pause all scanning" switch. This requires knowing all watchlists and toggling each via PATCH. We can implement a client-side "Pause all / Resume all" button using `api.watchlists.list()` and `update(id, { paused })` for each. This is functional. Or simpler: a "Manage watchlists" link. But "more options" — a pause-all switch is a real setting.

3. **Feed & display** — e.g., "Compact deal cards" toggle, "Show example/illustrative cards" no. These would require feed changes. Could store in localStorage and apply via a class or context, but wiring is extra. Maybe skip.

4. **Notifications** — add sub-toggles for "New deal alerts" and "Price-drop alerts" stored locally? Server pushes are controlled by scanner and not gated. Misleading. Instead add "Test notification" button? Could send a test FCM? There's no endpoint. Maybe add a "Notification schedule / quiet hours" — not implemented.

5. **Security** — "Change password" sends reset email via `/api/auth/forgot-password` with the user's email. Functional and useful. Add a button with confirmation toast. Also "Sign out of all devices" — could add endpoint to delete all AuthSessions except current. Maybe too much but doable. Let's consider.

6. **Data & privacy** — "Export my data" downloads a JSON of account, watchlists, alerts, profile, billing. Implement client-side by calling existing APIs. Functional. Add "Clear local cache" button (localStorage/sessionStorage + queryClient.clear) with toast. Useful.

7. **About / support** — app version, support email link, legal links (already). Could add "Contact support" mailto and "What's new" link. Light.

8. **Appearance** — dark mode is fixed, skip.

We should not overload. The user asked "add more" without specifics. A good approach: add 3–4 polished sections that are functional:
- Profile details (editable display name, email, verified badge, member since)
- Scanning (plan cadence summary, pause/resume all watchlists, manage watchlists link)
- Security (change password via reset email, sign out)
- Data & privacy (export data, clear local cache) — plus existing legal
- Keep notifications and danger zone.

We can `window.location.reload()` after save, or manage local state. Better: keep local `name` state initialized from `user.name`, and display it; header still shows old until reload. Could update the store? Simpler: after successful save, `toast.success` and `window.location.reload()`? That's heavy. Header uses `user` prop for name, not session. Saving name would need reload to update header. That's acceptable: after saving, we can call `window.location.reload()` or update via `router.refresh()` (Next app router) which re-fetches server component and updates user prop. `useRouter().refresh()` from next/navigation would work. Good. But is the settings panel under AppShell which receives user from server component; router.refresh re-renders server component and updates. We can do that.

However, adding a PATCH handler to profile route requires auth and DB update. Straightforward.

Now, what about "member since" — user.createdAt not in AuthUserView. We could extend AuthUserView and auth mapping. Maybe too much; could show plan info instead.

Let's design the settings additions with existing API and minimal backend:

**Section: Profile details**
- Name input (prefilled `user.name ?? ''`), email read-only with verified badge, "Save changes" button.
- PATCH `/api/profile` `{ name }` → update User.name. On success toast + `router.refresh()`.
- If name blank, save null? Let server accept empty string → null. Header falls back to email prefix.

**Section: Scanning**
- Fetch watchlists via `api.watchlists.list()`.
- Show: plan cadence ("Every 5 min on Pro"), active watchlist count, paused count.
- Toggle "Pause all scanning" (Switch) → PATCH each watchlist `{ paused: true/false }`, invalidate watchlists query, toast.
- Link/button "Manage watchlists" → setView('watchlists').
This is functional. Need `useQuery` for watchlists. Note `api.watchlists.list()` returns all watchlists; use queryKey ['watchlists'].
- If no watchlists, show "No watchlists yet" + button to create (setView('watchlists')).

**Section: Security**
- "Change password" button → POST `/api/auth/forgot-password` with user.email; toast "Reset link sent". For federated accounts? If user has passwordHash always (schema required), all have password. Fine. Rate limiting handled.
- "Sign out" already in account header. Could add "Sign out of this device" in security. Keep account sign out.
- Maybe "Active sessions" not available; skip.

**Section: Data & privacy**
- "Export my data" button → gather via APIs and download JSON:
  - `api.session.get()` (large), `api.watchlists.list()`, `api.profile.get()`, `api.alerts.list()`, `api.billing.get()`.
  - `api.listings.feed` maybe huge; skip or include saved listings? Could include only watchlists/profile/alerts/billing/session. Good enough.
  - Use Blob + anchor download `dealify-data-YYYY-MM-DD.json`.
- "Clear local cache" button → localStorage/sessionStorage clear? Careful: clearing localStorage would log the user out if token stored. We should not clear auth token. Instead clear only app-specific non-auth keys? Check `storedAuthTokenHeader` implementation. Could just `queryClient.clear()` + toast "Cached data refreshed" and `window.location.reload()`. That's safe. Call it "Refresh cached data".
- Existing legal links stay.

**Section: About**
- Version (from package.json? client can't import package.json easily? Next can import JSON). Could hardcode `v1.0.0` or use `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_VERSION`. Maybe skip.
- "Contact support" mailto:support@dealify.app, "Send feedback". Could add to Legal card footer. Light.

**Notifications**
- Keep PushOptIn. Add note about alert types (new listing / price drop) maybe with static badges. Could add a "Test push" button but no endpoint.
- Maybe add email alerts toggle — backend doesn't send email alerts. Skip.

This is a solid set. But the user might expect "settings" like toggles for notifications, appearance, etc. We can add a **Preferences** section with localStorage-backed toggles that actually affect the UI:
- "Compact feed cards" — would require feed component to read it. Could implement but touches feed layout. Maybe not.
- "Reduce motion" — add class `motion-reduce`? Tailwind's `motion-reduce` is media-based, not class. Could set `document.documentElement.classList.add('reduce-motion')` and add CSS overrides. Overkill.

Let's stick to functional settings.

remove “Live across 4 marketplaces” pill; add scrolling animation; make landing page professional/premium; make scanner constantly run at 10 min for Starter and 5 min for Pro. ## Decisions - Use extracted PNG logo assets rather than SVG: `public/logo.png` (600x159 lockup), `public/logo-mark.png` (254x256), `public/icon.png` (512x512). - Interpreted “scrolling animation” as scroll-triggered `FadeUp` reveals plus a marketplace marquee. - Scanner cadence is a plan floor: Starter 600s, Pro 300s, locked 3600s; slower stored watchlist intervals are still honored. - For settings expansion, prefer functional additions backed by existing/new APIs rather than decorative toggles. ## Work State ### Completed - Landing page polish: hero stats/status, filled phone feed examples, marketplaces strip, example deal cards, pricing/CTA trust rows, icon cards. - New logo wired into landing nav/footer, auth page (2 marks), marketing onboarding header, in-app header, in-app onboarding, and app-gate splash. - Metadata icons updated to `/icon.png` + `/logo-mark.png`. - Removed hero “Live across 4 marketplaces” pill. - Added `FadeUp` IntersectionObserver scroll reveal (reduced-motion safe) and seamless marketplace marquee with hover pause. - Scanner service now running detached under supervisor on port 3003; old scanner from `Codex/2026-11-09/ca/work/app` was stopped because it owned 3003 and used a different DB. - Fixed `supervisor.ts` path bug: replaced `new URL(...).pathname` with `fileURLToPath` so paths containing spaces work. - Installed missing `socket.io` in `mini-services/scanner-service`; first scan succeeded (14 listings), next scan scheduled +5 min. - Verified cadence: Starter 600s, Pro 300s, Pro trial 300s, locked 3600s. - TypeScript and ESLint clean after all edits. ### Active - Expanding `SettingsPanel` in `src/components/app/settings.tsx`; Now, how ambitious should we be? The user explicitly says "spend a lot of time on this." We should make substantial improvements. Let's plan a redesign of the funnel.

Given time/context constraints, we can make a significant, polished upgrade:

### Major upgrades

1. **Add a Review step** before account (new StepId 'review'), showing a complete blueprint with edit jump links. This is a big UX improvement and makes the flow feel complete.

2. **Persist draft answers + current step** in localStorage (`dealify.personalise-draft.v1`) so refresh doesn't lose progress. Restore on mount. Clear when continuing to account (after storing pending profile). Add a "Saved" indicator maybe.

3. **Header upgrade**: Add a 3-phase stepper (Preview / Personalise / Create account) with active state and completion ticks, plus "~2 min" estimate and a save indicator. Keep sign-in link. On mobile collapse to phase dots.

4. **Progress upgrade**: Replace simple bar with segmented progress + labels, maybe circular progress. Add question count and percentage. Keep Progress component but add milestone markers. Also make progress reflect prompts vs benefits differently? Simpler: segmented bar with 3 phases.

5. **Preview card upgrade**: Instead of static summary, make it dynamic:
   - Radar visual with sweeping animation (keep) and orbiting category emojis.
   - Add "estimated matches" count derived from selections (deterministic pseudo-count) and "live feed preview" with 2-3 example deals filtered to selected categories. Could derive from `stats.topDeals` if passed; but PersonalisationPreview doesn't receive stats. Pass stats.
   - Add checklist rows with edit buttons? Preview is not interactive on mobile; on desktop could have jump-to-step. Add `onEdit` callback and `steps` mapping? That adds complexity. Could make rows clickable to jump. Nice.
   - Show trial countdown / plan.

6. **Benefit screens redesign**:
   - benefit-scan: create a richer composition with animated scan ring, floating listing cards (3), live counter "3 deals matched in the last hour", "how it works" 3 steps. Use stats.
   - benefit-stories: already uses FlipStoriesPlayer; add "swipe" hint and stat strip. Maybe fine.
   - benefit-alerts: richer phone notification stack with timestamps and ROI badges; add "alerts run on Pro" note; add a mini toggle illustration.
   - Add a trust row common to benefit screens: "No card · Cancel anytime · 4 markets".
   - Add "benefit" step progress dots at top of content (1/3).

7. **Question steps polish**:
   - Add per-step icon + "Question X of Y" chip and estimated time.
   - Goal step: add "Most popular" badge on quick flips, selection ring, animated check, and a summary line at bottom ("We'll weight speed and margin").
   - Categories: add selected count chip, "Select all that apply", clear, and category card hover; add "Cars" recommended badge? Maybe not.
   - Budget: replace plain buttons with richer cards showing range and a descriptor; add a slider for custom? Keep inputs but style. Add a "typical flips in this range" hint.
   - Styles: chips with car silhouette icons? Could use lucide Car. Keep chips but add count and helper.
   - Makes: group by category with headers, selected chips at top. Current list can be long; improve with selected row and "popular" badges.
   - Location: add quick city suggestions (Sydney, Melbourne, London, New York, Toronto, Los Angeles) as chips; radius visualization; marketplace dropdown. Add "Anywhere" option.
   - Avoid: cards with icons (Store, Gauge, CalendarClock, Wrench) instead of plain.
   - Experience: cards with progress bars/levels and icons.
   - Add keyboard: Enter to continue (except in text inputs), ArrowLeft to go back maybe.

8. **Account step**: Add a "Your radar blueprint" recap (goal, categories, budget, location), trial timeline (Today: radar created → Day 7: trial ends → Pick plan), trust row, and CTA. Maybe add "What you get" list. Since it's the final step, make it feel rewarding: confetti-ish sparkles animation, "Radar ready" badge.

9. **Motion**: use AnimatePresence with better spring, stagger children. Respect reduced motion? framer's useReducedMotion could be used. Existing uses motion without guard. Could add `useReducedMotion` for large animations. Not critical.

10. **Mobile summary**: Add a compact sticky "blueprint" strip above footer on mobile showing selected goal/categories/budget count. Could clutter. Maybe add a collapsible summary sheet? Too much. Instead, on mobile preview is hidden; add a small "Your radar: 3 categories · $5k · Sydney" line in footer. Good.

11. **Add "Skip all personalisation"** link? There's already skip per optional step. Maybe add "I'll do this later" in header that goes to account step. That improves conversion. But account requires profile? `buildProfile` needs goal+experience; if skipped, pending profile removed, signup still works and in-app quiz is fallback. Add a subtle "Skip for now" in header that jumps to account with a note. Good.

12. **Validation messaging**: Show hint under disabled Continue ("Pick a goal to continue"). Add aria-live.

13. **Step transition direction**: keep.

14. **Auto-focus** the step heading on change for a11y.

15. **"Back" on first step** goes to landing? Could link home. Currently blank spacer. Maybe show a home/back-to-site link. Add.

16. **Header "Already have an account? Sign in"** keep.

17. **Use stats** for social proof in benefit screens and preview.

Implementation approach: Rewrite `onboarding-funnel.tsx` significantly. It's 1353 lines. We can edit targeted sections, but a lot changes. Maybe rewrite the whole file with improved components, preserving types/imports and behavior. That's risky but manageable. We can keep most existing step components and enhance.

Let's decide concrete scope to deliver high quality without breaking:

- Add `review` step + jump-to-step.
- Add localStorage draft persistence (answers + step).
- Redesign header with phase stepper and time estimate.
- Redesign progress area with segmented bar and labels.
- Enhance `PersonalisationPreview` with dynamic match estimate, category emojis orbiting radar, stats, and clickable rows to edit.
- Enhance benefit screens with richer visuals and shared trust row.
- Enhance question step shells with a `StepMeta` row (icon, "Question x of y", helper).
- Improve goal/categories/budget/location/avoid/experience visuals moderately.
- Improve account step with blueprint recap + timeline.
- Add mobile summary line in footer.
- Add keyboard Enter handling and focus management.
- Add skip-to-account in header.
- Add CSS for new elements (phase stepper, scan lines, preview deal rows, confetti/sparkle). Could use Tailwind classes mostly, minimal CSS additions.

Given the size, rewriting the file may be cleanest. But preserving imports and types is important. Let's design the new file structure carefully.

## Objective
- Finish polishing the Dealify signup/onboarding experience so it feels premium rather than basic, while preserving earlier settings, branding, landing, and scanner work.

## Requirements
- Latest request: “the onboarding is still very basic, make it much better. spend a lot of time on this.”
- Earlier requests, all completed: expand profile Settings; fix logo inside the app; add a matching left hero eyebrow on the landing page; make onboarding start from the beginning.
- Keep the onboarding aligned with the existing dark/orange/blue Dealify design language.

## Decisions
- Fully rewrote `onboarding-funnel.tsx` instead of incremental tweaks to deliver a noticeably richer flow.
- Added a 3-phase rail (Preview → Personalise → Account), segmented progress, question counters, estimated time left, and “Progress saved”.
- Added a dedicated Review step before account creation with jump-to-edit rows.
- Persist answers + current step in `localStorage` under `dealify.personalise-draft.v2`; clear the draft on account handoff after storing `dealify.pending-signup-profile.v1`.
- Reused the existing profile schema; added optional `avoidNote` free text to the funnel because `UserProfile.avoidNote` already exists.
- Preview/review/account now use live match estimates and example deals derived from selected categories/stats.
- Settings “Verified” badges use `bg-emerald-500/10` because `bg-emerald-400` is remapped to solid blue in `globals.css`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Logo wired into in-app header, in-app onboarding, and app-gate splash.
- Settings expanded: editable display name, scanning summary + pause/resume all, security reset link, data export/refresh, legal links, danger zone.
- Added `PATCH /api/profile` accepting `{ name }` and `api.profile.updateName`.
- Settings verified with tsc/ESLint and authenticated screenshots.
- Landing hero left eyebrow added: “STOP SCROLLING. START FLIPPING.”
- Onboarding funnel now starts at step 0 (intro benefit screen) instead of skipping to the first question.
- Full onboarding funnel rewrite completed in code with richer benefit screens, live radar preview, review step, grouped brands, quick cities, avoid-note input, account recap/timeline, and Enter-to-continue.

### Active
- Verify the rewritten `onboarding-funnel.tsx`: run TypeScript + ESLint, screenshot `/personalise` on desktop and mobile, and fix any rendering/typing issues.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run `bunx tsc --noEmit` and `bunx eslint src/components/landing/onboarding-funnel.tsx`.
2. Screenshot `/personalise` at 1440px and mobile width; step through benefits, goal, categories, budget, review, and account.
3. Verify draft restore, “Skip setup”, back navigation, Enter-to-continue, and account handoff.
4. Confirm `/personalise` and `/signup?mode=signup&personalised=1` return 200; fix any regressions.
5. If the user meant the in-app quiz too, apply a similar polish pass to `src/components/app/onboarding.tsx`.

## Relevant Files
- `src/components/landing/onboarding-funnel.tsx`: fully rewritten signup onboarding; needs verification.
- `src/components/app/settings.tsx`: expanded profile Settings panel.
- `src/app/api/profile/route.ts`: added `PATCH` display-name handler.
- `src/lib/api.ts`: `api.profile.updateName`, watchlists/alerts/billing/profile helpers.
- `src/components/landing/landing-page.tsx`: left hero eyebrow and landing polish.
- `src/app/globals.css`: `personalise-*` styles and emerald→blue remap.
- `src/components/app/onboarding.tsx`: in-app quiz; logo updated, possible future polish target.
- `src/components/app/header.tsx`: in-app header now uses `/logo.png`.
- `src/components/app/app-gate.tsx`: splash now uses `/logo-mark.png`.
- `src/components/signup/flip-stories.tsx`: benefit-stories player used by onboarding.
- `src/lib/profile-shared.ts`: onboarding option catalogs and profile types.

- `.zscripts/dev-3001.log`: dev server log.
- `.zscripts/scanner-3003.log`: scanner supervisor log.

## Important Context
- Dev server: `http://localhost:3001`; scanner health: `http://127.0.0.1:3003/health` returns `{"ok":true,"service":"dealify-scanner","port":3003,"mode":"gentle"}`.
- Scanner supervisor PID `94638`, child `94640`; plan cadence is Starter 600s, Pro 300s, locked 3600s.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish polishing the Dealify onboarding/signup funnel so it feels premium, then fix the "Start free trial" CTA so it opens onboarding rather than the sign-in/create-account page.

## Requirements
- Latest request: “when u click start free trial, it should take u to onboarding, not to the signin/create account page.”
- Earlier request: “the onboarding is still very basic, make it much better. spend a lot of time on this.”
- Preserve earlier settings, branding, landing, and scanner work; keep the dark/orange/blue Dealify design language.
- Onboarding must start from the beginning (intro benefit screen).

## Decisions
- Fully rewrote `src/components/landing/onboarding-funnel.tsx` with a 3-phase rail, segmented progress, question counters, time estimate, saved-progress badge, live radar preview, review step, account recap/timeline, and Enter-to-continue.
- Persist answers/step in `localStorage` under `dealify.personalise-draft.v2`; clear draft on account handoff after storing `dealify.pending-signup-profile.v1`.
- Reused the existing profile schema; `avoidNote` free text added because `UserProfile.avoidNote` exists.
- Replaced selected-state gradients with the CSS-driven dark/orange-tint look because `.personalise-step-shell` overrides selected backgrounds; `text-primary-foreground` made selected labels invisible.
- Centered short steps vertically (`lg:self-center` for prompt cards, `my-auto` for benefit/review/account).
- Added a sticky final CTA on the account step so it stays reachable on mobile.
- Sample preview deals now cover every vertical and filter by selected categories instead of falling back to cars.

## Work State
### Completed
- Onboarding funnel rewrite verified with `bunx tsc --noEmit` and `bunx eslint src/components/landing/onboarding-funnel.tsx` (both clean).
- Desktop (1440×1000) and mobile (390×844) walkthroughs of all 13 steps captured and reviewed.
- Fixed: selected budget/chip contrast, Popular/Most-popular badge overlap (now inline with `ml-auto`), preview Preferences false check, vertical balance, clipped preview trial card, muddy disabled CTA (`.dealify-cta:disabled` in `globals.css`), preview sample fallback, mobile "Skip" visibility, step-specific kickers, "Back to review" on account, sticky mobile CTA with safe-area padding.
- Behaviour tests passed: starts at benefit screen, draft persists/restores, “Progress saved” badge, Enter advances, Skip setup, Back to review, handoff to `/signup?mode=signup&personalised=1`, pending profile stored on full flow, draft cleared.
- `/personalise` and `/signup?mode=signup&personalised=1` both return 200.
- Landing page CTAs at `landing-page.tsx` lines 211, 252, 1119, 1239, 1302 already link to `/personalise`.

### Active
- Investigating the reported “Start free trial” destination: no obvious `/signup` CTA found yet in landing components; need to identify which CTA the user actually clicked (possibly in-app paywall/billing, auth page, or a redirect path).

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining “free trial” CTAs: `src/components/app/paywall.tsx` (`startTrial` at ~line 88, button ~203), `src/components/app/billing.tsx` (~325, ~470, ~543), and `src/components/landing/auth-page.tsx` (~688, ~758).
2. Check for redirects that could send a visitor from `/personalise` to `/signup` (e.g. `hasAccountMarker()` logic at `onboarding-funnel.tsx:342`, middleware, or app-gate paths).
3. Reproduce in the browser: clear storage, click each “Start free trial” CTA, and confirm the destination; change any `/signup` target to `/personalise`.
4. Re-run `bunx tsc --noEmit` and `bunx eslint` on touched files, then screenshot the fixed CTA path.

## Relevant Files
- `src/components/landing/onboarding-funnel.tsx`: rewritten signup funnel; most recent edits (kickers, sticky CTA, sample deals, badge alignment).
- `src/components/landing/landing-page.tsx`: all landing “Start free trial” links already point to `/personalise`.
- `src/components/app/paywall.tsx`: in-app “Start 7-day free trial” button (`startTrial`).
- `src/components/app/billing.tsx`: billing trial CTAs and plan cards.
- `src/components/landing/auth-page.tsx`: signup/login page with “Start 7-day free trial” submit button.
- `src/app/globals.css`: `personalise-*` styles, `.dealify-cta:disabled`, emerald→blue remap.
- `src/lib/profile-shared.ts`: onboarding option catalogs and profile types.
- `src/lib/landing-stats.ts`: live stats/deals used by the preview.
- `src/components/app/onboarding.tsx`: in-app quiz; already has segmented progress/step art, possible future polish target.
- `src/components/signup/flip-stories.tsx`: benefit-stories Remotion player.

## Important Context
- Dev server: `http://localhost:3001`; scanner health: `http://127.0.0.1:3003/health` → `{"ok":true,"service":"dealify-scanner","port":3003,"mode":"gentle"}`.
- `globals.css` deliberately remaps emerald classes to blue; avoid `bg-emerald-400` for translucent badges.

- `/personalise` passes `startAtPersonalisation` so it never redirects signed-in visitors.
- Auth sessions are currently `0`; user may need to sign in again.

- Root cause: saved onboarding draft could resume at the final "Create account" step, so "Start free trial" looked like it opened the signup page.

Fixed. The CTA itself was pointing at the right route — the problem was that the onboarding funnel was **restoring a saved draft that had stopped on the final “Create account” step**, so “Start free trial” looked like it dumped you straight onto the signup screen.

- **`src/components/landing/landing-page.tsx`** — every “Start free trial” / onboarding CTA now links to `/personalise?start=1` instead of `/personalise`.

87: const YEAR_WINDOW = 3
88: const YEAR_RATE = 0.025 // 2.5% of median per model year
89: const FALLBACK_KM_RATE = 2.2e-6 // fraction of median per km (~2.2% per 10,000 km)
90: const KM_RATE_MIN = 8e-7 // sanity bounds for a data-driven slope
91: const KM_RATE_MAX = 4e-6
92: const CONDITION_WEIGHT = 0.08 // full score ±1 → ±8% of value
93: const REGRESSION_MIN_COMPS = 6
94: const RECENCY_HALF_DAYS = 45 // weight 1.0 now → decays with listing age
95: 
96: function clamp(v: number, min: number, max: number): number {
97:   return Math.min(max, Math.max(min, v))
98: }
99: 
100: function median(values: number[]): number | null {
101:   if (values.length === 0) return null
102:   const sorted = [...values].sort((a, b) => a - b)
103:   const mid = Math.floor(sorted.length / 2)
104:   return sorted.length % 2 === 0 ? (sorted[mid - 1] + sorted[mid]) / 2 : sorted[mid]
105: }
106: 
107: /** Weighted median: accumulate weights until half the total is crossed */
108: function weightedMedian(entries: Array<{ value: number; weight: number }>): number | null {
109:   if (entries.length === 0) return null
110:   const sorted = [...entries].sort((a, b) => a.value - b.value)
111:   const total = sorted.reduce((s, e) => s + e.weight, 0)
112:   let acc = 0
113:   for (const e of sorted) {
114:     acc += e.weight
115:     if (acc >= total / 2) return e.value
116:   }
117:   return sorted[sorted.length - 1].value
118: }
119: 
120: /** Recency weight — current market data counts more than stale listings */
121: function recencyWeight(date: Date | null | undefined): number {
122:   if (!date) return 0.7
123:   const days = (Date.now() - date.getTime()) / 86_400_000
124:   if (days <= 30) return 1
125:   return Math.max(0.35, Math.pow(0.5, Math.max(0, days - 30) / RECENCY_HALF_DAYS))
126: }

179: /** True when the matched phrase is preceded by a negation ("has had no
180:  *  mechanical issues", "never had any accident damage" must NOT count as
181:  *  negative signals). Allows up to two filler words in between. */
182: function isNegated(haystack: string, m: RegExpMatchArray): boolean {
183:   if (m.index == null) return false
184:   const before = haystack.slice(Math.max(0, m.index - 24), m.index)
185:   return /\b(no|never|zero|without|hasn'?t|haven'?t|don'?t|doesn'?t|didn'?t|isn'?t|aren'?t)\s+(?:\w+\s+){0,2}$/i.test(before)
186: }
187: 
188: /** Short context snippet around a regex hit — the seller's own words */
189: function snippet(haystack: string, m: RegExpMatchArray): string {
190:   if (m.index == null) return m[0]
191:   const start = Math.max(0, m.index - 34)
192:   const end = Math.min(haystack.length, m.index + m[0].length + 34)
193:   let s = haystack.slice(start, end).replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim()
194:   if (start > 0) s = '…' + s
195:   if (end < haystack.length) s += '…'
196:   return s.length > 96 ? s.slice(0, 96) + '…' : s
197: }

199: export function analyzeCondition(input: {
200:   title: string
201:   description: string | null
202:   condition: string | null
203:   odometer: number | null
204:   year: number | null
205:   titleStatus: string | null
206: }): { score: number; signals: ConditionSignal[] } {
207:   const haystack = `${input.title}\n${input.description ?? ''}`
208:   let score = 0
209:   const signals: ConditionSignal[] = []
210: 
211:   for (const [re, label, impact] of POSITIVE_SIGNALS) {
212:     const m = haystack.match(re)
213:     if (m && !isNegated(haystack, m)) {
214:       score += impact
215:       signals.push({ label, impact, evidence: snippet(haystack, m) })
216:     }
217:   }
218:   for (const [re, label, impact] of NEGATIVE_SIGNALS) {
219:     const m = haystack.match(re)
220:     if (m && !isNegated(haystack, m)) {
221:       score += impact
222:       signals.push({ label, impact, evidence: snippet(haystack, m) })
223:     }
224:   }
225: 
226:   // Facebook listing condition field
227:   const cond = (input.condition ?? '').toUpperCase().replace(/[^A-Z]/g, '')
228:   if (cond === 'NEW') {
229:     score += 0.05
230:     signals.push({ label: 'Listed as new', impact: 0.05 })
231:   } else if (cond.startsWith('LIKENEW')) {
232:     score += 0.04
233:     signals.push({ label: 'Listed like-new', impact: 0.04 })
234:   } else if (cond === 'FAIR') {
235:     score -= 0.06
236:     signals.push({ label: 'Listed in fair condition', impact: -0.06 })
237:   }
238: 
239:   // Usage rate: AU average is ~13-15k km/year
240:   const thisYear = new Date().getFullYear()
241:   if (input.odometer != null && input.odometer > 1000 && input.year != null && input.year <= thisYear - 2) {
242:     const perYear = input.odometer / Math.max(1, thisYear - input.year)
243:     if (perYear < 10_000) {
244:       score += 0.05
245:       signals.push({ label: `Below-average usage (~${Math.round(perYear / 1000)}k km/yr)`, impact: 0.05 })
246:     } else if (perYear > 22_000) {
247:       score -= 0.05
248:       signals.push({ label: `Above-average usage (~${Math.round(perYear / 1000)}k km/yr)`, impact: -0.05 })
249:     }
250:   }
251: 
252:   if (input.titleStatus && /salvage|rebuilt|written|write|statutory/i.test(input.titleStatus)) {
253:     score -= 0.1
254:     signals.push({ label: `Title status: ${input.titleStatus}`, impact: -0.1 })
255:   }
256: 
257:   return { score: clamp(score, -1, 1), signals }
258: }

261: // Comp fetching + weighted statistics
262: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

264: interface Comp {
265:   id: string
266:   price: number
267:   odometer: number | null
268:   year: number | null
269:   sellerType: string | null
270:   weight: number
271:   date: Date | null
272: }
273: 
274: /** Trim/spec similarity boost: comps whose title shares distinctive words with
275:  *  the subject (trim badges like Wildtrak vs XL, spec words like dualcab) get
276:  *  up to +30% weight — same-model different-trim comps no longer count 1:1. */
277: const TRIM_WEIGHT_BOOST = 0.3
278: 
279: async function fetchComps(db: PrismaClient, input: ValuationInput): Promise<Comp[]> {
280:   if (!input.make || !input.model) return []
281: 
282:   const pool = await getCompPool(db)
283:   const candidates = filterComps(pool, input, YEAR_WINDOW, {
284:     currencyFloor,
285:   })
286: 
287:   const subjectTokens = titleTokens(
288:     input.title,
289:     input.make,
290:     input.model
291:   )
292:   const subjectTokenList = [...subjectTokens]
293: 
294:   const comps: Comp[] = []
295:   for (const c of candidates) {
296:     const date = c.postedAt ?? c.firstSeenAt
297:     let weight = recencyWeight(date)
298:     if (subjectTokenList.length > 0) {
299:       const compTokens = titleTokens(c.title, c.make, c.model)
300:       if (compTokens.size > 0) {
301:         let shared = 0
302:         for (const t of subjectTokenList) if (compTokens.has(t)) shared++
303:         const overlap = Math.min(1, shared / Math.min(subjectTokenList.length, compTokens.size))
304:         weight *= 1 + TRIM_WEIGHT_BOOST * overlap
305:       }
306:     }
307:     comps.push({
308:       id: c.id,
309:       price: c.price,
310:       odometer: c.odometer,
311:       year: c.year,
312:       sellerType: c.sellerType,
313:       weight,
314:       date,
315:     })
316:   }
317:   return comps
318: }

320: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
321: // Regression (price ~ odometer + year), weighted, solved with Cramer's rule
322: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
323: 
324: interface RegressionFit {
325:   intercept: number
326:   kmCoef: number // $ per km (negative)
327:   yearCoef: number // $ per year (positive)
328: }
329: 
330: function fitRegression(entries: Array<{ odo: number; year: number; price: number; w: number }>): RegressionFit | null {
331:   let n = 0
332:   let sx = 0
333:   let sy = 0
334:   let sxx = 0
335:   let syy = 0
336:   let sxy = 0
337:   let sp = 0
338:   let sxp = 0
339:   let syp = 0
340:   for (const e of entries) {
341:     const w = e.w
342:     n += w
343:     sx += w * e.odo
344:     sy += w * e.year
345:     sxx += w * e.odo * e.odo
346:     syy += w * e.year * e.year
347:     sxy += w * e.odo * e.year
348:     sp += w * e.price
349:     sxp += w * e.odo * e.price
350:     syp += w * e.year * e.price
351:   }
352:   // A = [[n, sx, sy], [sx, sxx, sxy], [sy, sxy, syy]], b = [sp, sxp, syp]
353:   const det3 = (
354:     a: number[][]
355:   ) =>
356:     a[0][0] * (a[1][1] * a[2][2] - a[1][2] * a[2][1]) -
357:     a[0][1] * (a[1][0] * a[2][2] - a[1][2] * a[2][0]) +
358:     a[0][2] * (a[1][0] * a[2][1] - a[1][1] * a[2][0])
359: 
360:   const A = [
361:     [n, sx, sy],
362:     [sx, sxx, sxy],
363:     [sy, sxy, syy],
364:   ]
365:   const det = det3(A)
366:   if (!isFinite(det) || Math.abs(det) < 1e-6) return null
367: 
368:   const replace = (col: number, b: number[]) => A.map((row, i) => row.map((v, j) => (j === col ? b[i] : v)))
369:   const intercept = det3(replace(0, [sp, sxp, syp])) / det
370:   const kmCoef = det3(replace(1, [sp, sxp, syp])) / det
371:   const yearCoef = det3(replace(2, [sp, sxp, syp])) / det
372:   if (!isFinite(intercept) || !isFinite(kmCoef) || !isFinite(yearCoef)) return null
373:   return { intercept, kmCoef, yearCoef }
374: }

376: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
377: // Main entry: estimate the market value of one vehicle
378: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
379: 
380: export async function estimateValue(db: PrismaClient, input: ValuationInput): Promise<ValuationResult | null> {
381:   const comps = await fetchComps(db, input)
382:   if (comps.length === 0 || input.price === null) return null
383: 
384:   const rawPrices = comps.map((c) => c.price)
385:   const rawMedian = median(rawPrices) ?? comps[0].price
386:   const rawAvg = rawPrices.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / rawPrices.length
387:   const sortedPrices = [...rawPrices].sort((a, b) => a - b)
388:   const rawLow = sortedPrices[Math.floor(sortedPrices.length * 0.1)]
389:   const rawHigh = sortedPrices[Math.floor(sortedPrices.length * 0.9)]
390: 
391:   const wMedian = weightedMedian(comps.map((c) => ({ value: c.price, weight: c.weight }))) ?? rawMedian
392: 
393:   const odoComps = comps.filter((c) => c.odometer != null)
394:   const compsWithOdometer = odoComps.length
395:   const totalWeight = comps.reduce((s, c) => s + c.weight, 0)
396:   const wAvg = (pick: (c: Comp) => number | null): number | null => {
397:     let acc = 0
398:     let wsum = 0
399:     for (const c of comps) {
400:       const v = pick(c)
401:       if (v == null) continue
402:       acc += v * c.weight
403:       wsum += c.weight
404:     }
405:     return wsum > 0 ? acc / wsum : null
406:   }
407:   const compsAvgOdometer = wAvg((c) => c.odometer)
408:   const compsAvgYear = wAvg((c) => c.year)
409:   const dealerComps = comps.filter((c) => (c.sellerType ?? '').toUpperCase().includes('DEAL')).length
410:   const privateComps = comps.length - dealerComps
411: 
412:   let method: ValuationMethod = 'median'
413:   let baseEstimate = wMedian
414:   let odometerRatePerKm = rawMedian * FALLBACK_KM_RATE
415: 
416:   // Data-driven price-per-km slope (single variable) — used by the
417:   // weighted-comps method and as the fallback display rate
418:   let dataKmRate: number | null = null
419:   if (odoComps.length >= 4) {
420:     const odoSpread = Math.max(...odoComps.map((c) => c.odometer!)) - Math.min(...odoComps.map((c) => c.odometer!))
421:     if (odoSpread > 30_000) {
422:       // weighted covariance / variance
423:       let mx = 0
424:       let my = 0
425:       let wsum = 0
426:       for (const c of odoComps) {
427:         mx += c.weight * c.odometer!
428:         my += c.weight * c.price
429:         wsum += c.weight
430:       }
431:       mx /= wsum
432:       my /= wsum
433:       let cov = 0
434:       let varr = 0
435:       for (const c of odoComps) {
436:         cov += c.weight * (c.odometer! - mx) * (c.price - my)
437:         varr += c.weight * (c.odometer! - mx) ** 2
438:       }
439:       if (varr > 0) {
440:         const slope = cov / varr // $ per km, expected negative
441:         const rate = -slope
442:         const rMin = rawMedian * KM_RATE_MIN
443:         const rMax = rawMedian * KM_RATE_MAX
444:         if (rate >= rMin && rate <= rMax) dataKmRate = rate
445:       }
446:     }
447:   }
448: 
449:   const subjectOdo = input.odometer && input.odometer > 0 ? input.odometer : null
450:   const subjectYear = input.year
451: 
452:   // Method 1: weighted OLS regression when there is enough odometer data.
453:   // Outlier-trimmed first: comps priced outside the P10–P90 band (typos,
454:   // wrecked-price outliers) would otherwise skew the slope.
455:   if (odoComps.length >= REGRESSION_MIN_COMPS && comps.length >= REGRESSION_MIN_COMPS) {
456:     const fitInput =
457:       comps.length >= 8
458:         ? odoComps.filter((c) => c.price >= rawLow && c.price <= rawHigh)
459:         : odoComps
460:     if (fitInput.length >= REGRESSION_MIN_COMPS) {
461:       const fit = fitRegression(
462:         fitInput.map((c) => ({
463:           odo: c.odometer!,
464:           year: c.year ?? compsAvgYear ?? subjectYear ?? 2015,
465:           price: c.price,
466:           w: c.weight,
467:         }))
468:       )
469:       if (fit) {
470:         const rate = -fit.kmCoef
471:         const rMin = rawMedian * KM_RATE_MIN
472:         const rMax = rawMedian * KM_RATE_MAX
473:         const yearCoefOk = fit.yearCoef >= 0 && fit.yearCoef <= rawMedian * 0.05
474:         if (rate >= rMin && rate <= rMax && yearCoefOk) {
475:           const x1 = subjectOdo ?? odoComps.reduce((s, c) => s + c.odometer!, 0) / odoComps.length
476:           const x2 = subjectYear ?? compsAvgYear ?? 2015
477:           const predicted = fit.intercept + fit.kmCoef * x1 + fit.yearCoef * x2
478:           // clamp extrapolation to a sane band around the market
479:           const clamped = clamp(predicted, wMedian * 0.55, wMedian * 1.5)
480:           if (clamped > 1000) {
481:             method = 'regression'
482:             baseEstimate = clamped
483:             odometerRatePerKm = rate
484:           }
485:         }
486:       }
487:     }
488:   }
489: 
490:   // Method 2: odometer/year-normalized weighted comps (hedonic adjustment)
491:   if (method === 'median') {
492:     const rate = dataKmRate ?? rawMedian * FALLBACK_KM_RATE
493:     odometerRatePerKm = rate
494:     if (subjectOdo != null && compsWithOdometer >= 2) {
495:       const adjusted = comps.map((c) => ({
496:         value:
497:           c.price +
498:           (c.odometer != null ? (c.odometer - subjectOdo) * rate : 0) +
499:           (subjectYear != null && c.year != null ? (subjectYear - c.year) * YEAR_RATE * wMedian : 0),
500:         weight: c.odometer != null ? c.weight : c.weight * 0.8,
501:       }))
502:       const adjMedian = weightedMedian(adjusted)
503:       if (adjMedian != null && adjMedian > 1000) {
504:         method = 'weighted-comps'
505:         baseEstimate = clamp(adjMedian, wMedian * 0.55, wMedian * 1.5)
506:       }

269: /** Similarity for a generic comp (0..1) — shared-token density, capped:
270:  *  enough for the UI's comp list to rank near-identical items first. */
271: function genericSimilarity(subjectTokens: string[], compTokens: string[]): number {
272:   if (subjectTokens.length === 0 || compTokens.length === 0) return 0.3
273:   const shared = subjectTokens.filter((t) => compTokens.includes(t)).length
274:   const union = new Set([...subjectTokens, ...compTokens]).size
275:   return Math.max(0.3, Math.min(1, shared / Math.max(1, union) + 0.25))

17:  *   L2  make curve     — log-linear price-vs-age fit on the make's local

60: async function loadSoldPool(db: PrismaClient): Promise<SoldRow[]> {
61:   const rows = await db.listing.findMany({
62:     where: {
63:       status: 'stale',
64:       isScam: false,
65:       price: { not: null, gt: 500 },
66:     },
67:     select: {
68:       id: true,
69:       make: true,
70:       model: true,
71:       year: true,
72:       price: true,
73:       currency: true,
74:       previousPrice: true,
75:       firstSeenAt: true,
76:       lastSeenAt: true,
77:       postedAt: true,
78:     },
79:   })
80:   return rows.flatMap((r) => {
81:     if (r.price == null) return []
82:     const basis = r.postedAt ?? r.firstSeenAt
83:     const days = Math.max(1, Math.round((r.lastSeenAt.getTime() - basis.getTime()) / 86_400_000))
84:     return [{
85:       id: r.id,
86:       make: r.make ?? '',
87:       model: r.model ?? '',
88:       year: r.year,
89:       price: r.price,
90:       currency: r.currency ?? 'AUD',
91:       previousPrice: r.previousPrice,
92:       firstSeenAt: r.firstSeenAt,
93:       lastSeenAt: r.lastSeenAt,
94:       postedAt: r.postedAt,
95:       daysOnMarket: days,
96:     }]

100: /** Cached sold pool — invalidated when the stale-listing count changes. */
101: export async function getSoldPool(db: PrismaClient): Promise<SoldRow[]> {
102:   const rowCount = await db.listing.count({ where: { status: 'stale', isScam: false, price: { gt: 500 } } })
103:   if (soldCache && soldCache.rowCount === rowCount && Date.now() - soldCache.loadedAt < SOLD_POOL_TTL_MS) {
104:     return soldCache.rows
105:   }
106:   const rows = await loadSoldPool(db)
107:   soldCache = { rowCount, loadedAt: Date.now(), rows }
108:   return rows
109: }

115: function median(values: number[]): number | null {
116:   if (values.length === 0) return null
117:   const sorted = [...values].sort((a, b) => a - b)
118:   const mid = Math.floor(sorted.length / 2)
119:   return sorted.length % 2 === 0 ? (sorted[mid - 1] + sorted[mid]) / 2 : sorted[mid]
120: }
121: 
122: function quantile(values: number[], q: number): number | null {
123:   if (values.length === 0) return null
124:   const sorted = [...values].sort((a, b) => a - b)
125:   const idx = Math.min(sorted.length - 1, Math.max(0, Math.round((sorted.length - 1) * q)))
126:   return sorted[idx]
127: }

129: function round50(n: number): number {
130:   return Math.max(0, Math.round(n / 50) * 50)

147: export function soldIntelFor(soldPool: SoldRow[], subject: {
148:   make: string | null
149:   model: string | null
150:   currency?: string | null
151: }): SoldIntel {
152:   const make = normalizeKey(subject.make)
153:   const model = normalizeKey(subject.model)
154:   const cur = (subject.currency ?? 'AUD').toUpperCase()
155:   const empty: SoldIntel = { count: 0, medianPrice: null, medianDaysToSell: null, askingGapPct: null, sample: [] }
156:   if (!make || !model) return empty
157:   const rows = soldPool.filter(
158:     (s) =>
159:       normalizeKey(s.make) === make &&
160:       normalizeKey(s.model) === model &&
161:       s.currency.toUpperCase() === cur &&
162:       s.price >= currencyFloor(s.currency)
163:   )
164:   if (rows.length === 0) return empty
165:   const dropped = rows.filter((s) => s.previousPrice != null && s.previousPrice > s.price)
166:   const gaps = dropped.map((s) => (s.previousPrice! - s.price) / s.previousPrice!)
167:   return {
168:     count: rows.length,
169:     medianPrice: median(rows.map((s) => s.price)),
170:     medianDaysToSell: median(rows.map((s) => s.daysOnMarket)),
171:     askingGapPct: gaps.length >= 2 ? Math.round((gaps.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / gaps.length) * 100) : null,
172:     sample: rows.slice(0, 3).map((s) => ({ title: `${s.year ?? ''} ${s.make} ${s.model}`.trim(), price: s.price, daysOnMarket: s.daysOnMarket })),
173:   }

212: export interface IntelSubject {
213:   id: string
214:   make: string | null
215:   model: string | null
216:   year: number | null
217:   price: number | null
218:   currency?: string | null
219:   /** an already-computed live-comp valuation (estimatedValue + count) from
220:    *  valuation.ts — reused as the L1 anchor so the two engines never
221:    *  disagree about the comp median */
222:   valuation?: { value: number; compCount: number } | null

225: interface CurveFit {
226:   /** predicted log-price at age (intercept form) */
227:   predict: (age: number) => number
228:   rows: number
229:   ageSpread: number
230: }
231: 
232: /** Robust log(price) ~ age fit (Theil–Sen: the MEDIAN of pairwise slopes,
233:  *  so one parts-grade $1,000 outlier can't drag the whole make curve — OLS
234:  *  let a single wreck reprice every Audi). Needs an age spread to be a curve
235:  *  at all; slope clamped to sane depreciation (allows gentle classic-car
236:  *  appreciation, forbids noise). */
237: function fitAgeCurve(rows: Array<{ price: number; age: number }>): CurveFit | null {
238:   const usable = rows
239:     .filter((r) => r.age >= 0 && r.age <= 60 && r.price > 0 && Number.isFinite(r.price))
240:     .map((r) => ({ age: r.age, logP: Math.log(r.price) }))
241:   if (usable.length < 6) return null
242:   const ages = usable.map((r) => r.age)
243:   const meanAge = ages.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / ages.length
244:   const spread = Math.sqrt(ages.reduce((s, a) => s + (a - meanAge) ** 2, 0) / ages.length)
245:   if (spread < 1.5) return null // one-model-year cluster — no curve to fit
246: 
247:   // Theil–Sen slope: median over pairs with a real age difference
248:   const slopes: number[] = []
249:   for (let i = 0; i < usable.length; i++) {
250:     for (let j = i + 1; j < usable.length; j++) {
251:       const dAge = usable[j].age - usable[i].age
252:       if (Math.abs(dAge) < 1) continue
253:       slopes.push((usable[j].logP - usable[i].logP) / dAge)
254:     }
255:   }
256:   if (slopes.length < 6) return null
257:   let slope = median(slopes) ?? 0
258:   slope = Math.min(0.04, Math.max(-0.35, slope)) // clamp: strong decay OK, noise-appreciation not
259:   // intercept: median of per-point intercepts (outlier-robust anchor)
260:   const intercept = median(usable.map((r) => r.logP - slope * r.age)) ?? 0
261:   return {
262:     predict: (age: number) => intercept + slope * Math.min(60, Math.max(0, age)),
263:     rows: usable.length,
264:     ageSpread: spread,
265:   }
266: }

268: function ageOf(year: number | null): number | null {
269:   if (year == null || year < 1930 || year > new Date().getFullYear() + 1) return null
270:   return new Date().getFullYear() - year
271: }

273: function liquidityClassFor(days: number): MarketIntel['liquidityClass'] {
274:   if (days <= 21) return 'fast'
275:   if (days <= 42) return 'normal'
276:   if (days <= 60) return 'slow'
277:   return 'very-slow'
278: }

283:       return `${compCount} live ${compCount === 1 ? 'comp' : 'comps'}`
284:     case 'sold-comps':
285:       return `${soldCount} recently sold + ${compCount} live`
286:     case 'make-curve':

288:     case 'market-baseline':

293: /**
294:  * The evidence ladder. Always returns a value (except when nothing at all is
295:  * known — no year for the curve, non-AUD market for the baseline), with the
296:  * basis and confidence that provenance deserves.
297:  */
298: export async function computeMarketIntel(
299:   db: PrismaClient,
300:   subject: IntelSubject
301: ): Promise<MarketIntel | null> {
302:   const make = subject.make
303:   const model = subject.model
304:   const currency = (subject.currency ?? 'AUD').toUpperCase()
305:   const floor = currencyFloor(currency)
306:   const isAud = currency === 'AUD'
307: 
308:   const [activePool, soldPool] = await Promise.all([getCompPool(db), getSoldPool(db)])
309:   const sold = soldIntelFor(soldPool, { make, model, currency })
310: 
311:   const sameMakeRows = activePool.filter(
312:     (c) => normalizeKey(c.make) === normalizeKey(make) && c.currency.toUpperCase() === currency && c.price >= floor
313:   )
314:   const sameFamilyRows = sameMakeRows.filter((c) => normalizeKey(c.model) === normalizeKey(model))
315: 
316:   const factors: IntelFactor[] = []
317:   const age = ageOf(subject.year)
318:   const askingGapPct = sold.askingGapPct ?? ASKING_TO_SALE_DISCOUNT_PCT
319: 
320:   // ---- L1: live comps (asking prices, gap-discounted) ------------------
321:   let compCount = 0
322:   let liveMedian: number | null = null
323:   let iqrPct: number | null = null
324:   if (make && model) {
325:     if (subject.valuation && subject.valuation.compCount >= 3) {
326:       // reuse the professional valuation's estimate (it already applies
327:       // year/odometer adjustments) as the L1 anchor
328:       compCount = subject.valuation.compCount
329:       liveMedian = subject.valuation.value
330:     } else {
331:       const comps = filterComps(
332:         activePool,
333:         { id: subject.id, make, model, year: subject.year, currency },
334:         4 // generation window — wider than the strict ±3 of market stats
335:       )
336:       if (comps.length >= 3) {
337:         compCount = comps.length
338:         liveMedian = median(comps.map((c) => c.price))
339:         const q1 = quantile(comps.map((c) => c.price), 0.25)
340:         const q3 = quantile(comps.map((c) => c.price), 0.75)
341:         if (q1 != null && q3 != null && liveMedian != null && liveMedian > 0) {
342:           iqrPct = Math.round(((q3 - q1) / liveMedian) * 100)
343:         }
344:       }
345:     }
346:   }
347: 
348:   // ---- decide the basis ladder -----------------------------------------
349:   let value: number | null = null
350:   let basis: ValueBasis = 'market-baseline'
351:   let confidence: IntelConfidence = 'low'
352: 
353:   if (liveMedian != null && compCount >= 3) {
354:     // L1 — discount the asking median into a sale-value estimate
355:     value = liveMedian * (1 - askingGapPct / 100)
356:     basis = 'live-comps'
357:     confidence = compCount >= 6 && (iqrPct == null || iqrPct <= 45) ? 'high' : 'medium'
358:     if (sold.count >= 2 && sold.medianPrice != null) {
359:       // L1S — sold evidence outranks asking evidence: blend, sold-weighted
360:       const wSold = Math.min(0.7, sold.count / (sold.count + compCount))
361:       value = wSold * sold.medianPrice + (1 - wSold) * value
362:       basis = 'sold-comps'
363:       confidence = 'high'
364:     }
365:     factors.push({
366:       label: compCount > 0 ? `${compCount} live ${compCount === 1 ? 'comp' : 'comps'} on the market` : 'Live comps',
367:       detail:
368:         sold.count >= 2 && sold.medianPrice != null
369:           ? `Active asking median ${Math.round(liveMedian).toLocaleString()} + ${sold.count} recently sold at ~${Math.round(sold.medianPrice).toLocaleString()}`
370:           : `Asking median ${Math.round(liveMedian).toLocaleString()}, less the typical ${askingGapPct}% asking→sale gap`,
371:     })
372:   } else if (sold.count >= 2 && sold.medianPrice != null) {
373:     // sold comps only — no live market to compare against
374:     value = sold.medianPrice
375:     basis = 'sold-comps'
376:     confidence = sold.count >= 4 ? 'high' : 'medium'
377:     factors.push({
378:       label: `${sold.count} recently sold`,
379:       detail: `Sold median ~${Math.round(sold.medianPrice).toLocaleString()} (left the market under our watch)`,
380:     })
381:   } else if (age != null && make) {
382:     // ---- L2: make curve over local rows (active + sold) ---------------
383:     const curveRows = [
384:       ...sameMakeRows.map((c) => ({ price: c.price, age: ageOf(c.year) })),
385:       ...soldPool
386:         .filter((s) => normalizeKey(s.make) === normalizeKey(make) && s.currency.toUpperCase() === currency)
387:         .map((s) => ({ price: s.price, age: ageOf(s.year) })),
388:     ]
389:     const fit = fitAgeCurve(curveRows.filter((r): r is { price: number; age: number } => r.age != null))
390:     if (fit) {
391:       let curveValue = Math.exp(fit.predict(age))
392:       // guard-rail: no single prediction may stray absurdly far from the
393:       // make's own median — a curve is structure, not a repricing event
394:       const makeMedian = median(sameMakeRows.map((c) => c.price))
395:       if (makeMedian != null && makeMedian > 0) {
396:         curveValue = Math.min(makeMedian * 2.2, Math.max(makeMedian * 0.45, curveValue))
397:       }
398:       value = curveValue
399:       basis = 'make-curve'
400:       confidence = fit.rows >= 10 ? 'medium' : 'low'
401:       factors.push({
402:         label: 'Make depreciation curve',
403:         detail: `Fit on ${fit.rows} local ${make} prices across ${Math.round(fit.ageSpread)} yrs of model ages`,
404:       })
405:     } else if (isAud) {
406:       // ---- L4: curated AU baseline (L3 global-curve adds little at this
407:       //      pool size — the baseline is better-calibrated) --------------
408:       const prior = auBaselineValue(make, age)
409:       if (prior) {
410:         value = prior.value
411:         basis = 'market-baseline'
412:         confidence = 'low'
413:         factors.push({
414:           label: 'AU market baseline',
415:           detail: prior.generic
416:             ? `Typical ${age}-year-old value band — no ${make} comps locally yet`
417:             : `Typical ${age}-year-old ${make} private-sale band — no local comps yet`,
418:         })
419:       }
420:     }
421:   } else if (isAud && make) {
422:     const prior = auBaselineValue(make, 10)
423:     if (prior) {
424:       value = prior.value
425:       basis = 'market-baseline'
426:       confidence = 'low'
427:       factors.push({ label: 'AU market baseline', detail: `Rough ${make} value band — no model year to age it` })
428:     }
429:   }
430: 
431:   if (value == null || value < floor * 0.5) return null
432:   value = round50(value)
433: 
434:   // ---- liquidity + resale ----------------------------------------------
435:   const liquidityDays = sold.count >= 2 ? sold.medianDaysToSell : null
436:   const expectedDaysToSell = liquidityDays ?? auBaselineDaysToSell(make)
437:   const resaleEstimate =
438:     sold.count >= 2 && sold.medianPrice != null
439:       ? round50(sold.medianPrice)
440:       : round50(value * (1 - askingGapPct / 100))
441:   if (sold.count > 0 && sold.medianDaysToSell != null) {
442:     factors.push({
443:       label: 'Sells in ~' + Math.round(sold.medianDaysToSell) + ' days',
444:       detail: `Median time-on-market across ${sold.count} recently sold ${make ?? ''} ${model ?? ''}`.trim(),
445:     })
446:   }
447: 
448:   const bandPct = confidence === 'high' ? 15 : confidence === 'medium' ? 22 : 30
449:   return {
450:     value,
451:     low: round50(value * (1 - bandPct / 100)),
452:     high: round50(value * (1 + bandPct / 100)),
453:     confidence,
454:     basis,
455:     basisLabel: basisLabelFor(basis, compCount, sold.count),
456:     compCount,
457:     soldCompCount: sold.count,
458:     iqrPct,
459:     liquidityDays,
460:     liquidityClass: liquidityDays != null ? liquidityClassFor(liquidityDays) : null,
461:     expectedDaysToSell: Math.round(expectedDaysToSell),
462:     resaleEstimate,
463:     resaleBasis: sold.count >= 2 ? 'sold-comps' : 'asking-gap',
464:     askingGapPct,
465:     factors,
466:   }
467: }

488: /** Ratio bands on asking/fairValue (unchanged vocabulary), gated by the
489:  *  strength of the evidence behind fairValue. A claim is only as strong as
490:  *  the data it stands on: "exceptional" needs real comps or sold proof. */
491: export function rateWithEvidence(
492:   asking: number,
493:   fairValue: number,
494:   profitable: boolean,
495:   evidence: RatingEvidence
496: ): RatedDeal | null {
497:   if (!(fairValue > 0) || !(asking > 0)) return null
498:   const ratio = asking / fairValue
499:   let rating: DealRatingV2
500:   if (ratio <= 0.65) rating = 'exceptional'
501:   else if (ratio <= 0.78) rating = 'excellent'
502:   else if (ratio <= 0.9) rating = 'good'
503:   else if (ratio <= 1.05) rating = 'fair'
504:   else rating = 'poor'
505: 
506:   const notes: string[] = []
507:   const realEvidence = evidence.compCount >= 4 || evidence.soldCompCount >= 2
508: 
509:   // Gate 1 — top ratings need real evidence, never a baseline guess
510:   if (rating === 'exceptional' && (!realEvidence || evidence.confidence === 'low')) {
511:     rating = 'excellent'
512:     notes.push(
513:       evidence.confidence === 'low'
514:         ? 'Value is still a market-baseline estimate — top rating withheld until comps or sold evidence lands'
515:         : 'Too few comps or sold observations to certify "exceptional"'
516:     )
517:   }
518:   // Gate 2 — low-confidence values cap at good
519:   if (evidence.confidence === 'low' && (rating === 'exceptional' || rating === 'excellent')) {
520:     rating = 'good'
521:     notes.push('Capped at "good" — the value estimate is low-confidence until local data grows')
522:   }
523:   // Gate 3 — measured slow market caps at good (car won't turn over)
524:   if (
525:     evidence.liquidityDays != null &&
526:     evidence.liquidityDays > 60 &&
527:     (rating === 'exceptional' || rating === 'excellent')
528:   ) {
529:     rating = 'good'
530:     notes.push(`Capped at "good" — this family takes ~${Math.round(evidence.liquidityDays)} days to sell locally`)
531:   }
532:   // Gate 4 — underpriced is not profitable (unchanged from v1)
533:   if (!profitable && (rating === 'exceptional' || rating === 'excellent' || rating === 'good')) {
534:     rating = 'fair'
535:     notes.push('Below market value, but repairs + costs + contingency eat the margin')
536:   }
537:   return { rating, notes }
538: }

7:  *   1. collect            — the listing row itself (scanned live from FB AU)
8:  *   2. comparables        — generation / variant / transmission / mileage /
9:  *                           local-market matched comp set + price stats
10:  *   3. fair market value  — gradient-boosted model prediction blended with
11:  *                           the live-comp valuation, with an honest
12:  *                           confidence grade and value band
13:  *   4. condition/repairs  — evidence-locked recon estimate from the ad's own
14:  *                           words (mechanical / cosmetic / tyres / service /
15:  *                           inspection), via the flip-plan step engine
16:  *   5. flip potential     — expected resale − purchase target − repairs −
17:  *                           transaction costs − contingency allowance
18:  *   6. ranking facts      — net margin, confidence, comparable listings and
19:  *                           the concrete reasons the car may be underpriced
20:  *
21:  * The key distinction, encoded structurally: a car priced below market value
22:  * is NOT automatically profitable to flip — `valueVerdict` (price vs fair
23:  * value) is kept separate from `profitable` (margin after repairs, costs and
24:  * contingency). The rating gate in scoring.ts only lets margin-positive
25:  * listings through as good-ROI deals.
26:  */
27:

138: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
139: // Transaction costs + contingency (flip underwriting — market-agnostic)
140: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
141: 
142: /** Asking→realized haircut for a flipped car: fair value is a median of ASKING
143:  *  prices, private sales transact below asking, and a flipper sells at a small
144:  *  discount for speed. Mirrors the generic path's 12% haircut. */
145: export const CAR_REALIZED_SALE_PCT = 0.92
146: 
147: /** listing sundries (ads, detailing supplies, transfer/registration papers)
148:  * plus the estimated transfer/registration bite on purchase — scales with
149:  * price in the listing's own currency (a sane estimate in every market:
150:  * ~3% transfer-ish cost capped, plus a small fixed sundry block) */
151: export function transactionCosts(purchase: number): number {
152:   const transfer = Math.min(600, Math.max(150, Math.round(purchase * 0.03)))
153:   return 120 + transfer
154: }
155: 
156: /** contingency allowance — the unplanned (a PPI surprise, a gearbox flush,
157:  * a blown tyre on the test drive). 5% of purchase, floored at $250. */
158: export function contingencyAllowance(purchase: number): number {
159:   return Math.max(250, Math.round(purchase * 0.05))
160: }
161: 
162: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
163: // Fair-value blend
164: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
165: 
166: function round50(n: number): number {
167:   return Math.max(0, Math.round(n / 50) * 50)
168: }
169: 
170: /** Keep negative margins negative; the market-value helper above is floored. */
171: function round50Signed(n: number): number {
172:   return Math.round(n / 50) * 50
173: }
174: 
175: function clamp(v: number, min: number, max: number): number {
176:   return Math.min(max, Math.max(min, v))
177: }

179: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
180: // Reasons the car may be underpriced (step 6)
181: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

183: function buildReasonsUnderpriced(
184:   listing: AnalyzableListing,
185:   fairValue: number,
186:   asking: number,
187:   comps: ComparableListing[],
188:   compStats: ComparableStats,
189:   discountPct: number,
190:   errorBandPct: number,
191:   currency: string | null
192: ): string[] {
193:   const money = (n: number) => formatMoneyCurrency(n, currency)
194:   const reasons: string[] = []
195:   if (discountPct > errorBandPct) {
196:     reasons.push(
197:       `Asking ${money(asking)} is ${Math.round(discountPct)}% below the estimated fair value of ${money(fairValue)} — outside the ±${Math.round(errorBandPct)}% error band, i.e. a genuine underprice, not noise`
198:     )
199:   }
200:   if (compStats.count >= 3 && compStats.low25 != null && asking < compStats.low25) {
201:     reasons.push(
202:       `Cheapest comparable on the local market: ${compStats.count} similar cars, the 25th-percentile comp is ${money(compStats.low25)} and this one is ${money(asking)}`
203:     )
204:   }
205:   if (compStats.median != null && compStats.count >= 3 && asking < compStats.median) {
206:     const gap = Math.round(((compStats.median - asking) / compStats.median) * 100)
207:     if (gap > 8) {
208:       reasons.push(
209:         `${money(compStats.median - asking)} under the comparable-set median (${money(compStats.median)}) across ${compStats.count} matched comps`
210:       )
211:     }
212:   }
213:   if (listing.previousPrice != null && listing.price != null && listing.previousPrice > listing.price) {
214:     reasons.push(
215:       `Price already dropped ${money(listing.previousPrice - listing.price)} (${Math.round(((listing.previousPrice - listing.price) / listing.previousPrice) * 100)}%) — a seller who has moved once will move again`
216:     )
217:   }
218:   const dom = daysOnMarket(listing)
219:   if (dom != null && dom >= 21) {
220:     reasons.push(
221:       `${dom} days on market — past the fresh-listing window, so negotiation leverage sits with the buyer`
222:     )
223:   }
224:   const kmComps = compStats.avgOdometer
225:   if (listing.odometer != null && kmComps != null && kmComps > 0 && listing.odometer < kmComps * 0.75) {
226:     reasons.push(
227:       `${Math.round((kmComps - listing.odometer) / 1000)}k km less than the comparable average (${Math.round(kmComps / 1000)}k km)`
228:     )
229:   }
230:   if ((listing.sellerType ?? '').toUpperCase().includes('INDIVIDUAL') || !listing.sellerType) {
231:     reasons.push('Private seller — no dealer margin floor, no recon to charge for, and no floor price to defend')
232:   }
233:   return reasons.slice(0, 6)
234: }
235: 
236: function daysOnMarket(l: AnalyzableListing): number | null {
237:   const from = l.postedAt ?? l.firstSeenAt
238:   if (!from) return null
239:   return Math.max(0, Math.floor((Date.now() - from.getTime()) / 86_400_000))
240: }

274: function buildRepairEstimate(steps: FlipStep[]): {
275:   items: RepairItem[]
276:   totalLow: number
277:   totalMid: number
278:   totalHigh: number
279: } {
280:   const items: RepairItem[] = steps.map((st) => ({
281:     id: st.id,
282:     title: st.title,
283:     category: STEP_CATEGORY[st.id] ?? 'mechanical',
284:     costLow: st.costLow,
285:     costMid: st.costMid,
286:     costHigh: st.costHigh,
287:     evidence: st.why,
288:   }))
289:   const sum = (pick: (i: RepairItem) => number) => items.reduce((s, i) => s + pick(i), 0)
290:   return {
291:     items,
292:     totalLow: sum((i) => i.costLow),
293:     totalMid: sum((i) => i.costMid),
294:     totalHigh: sum((i) => i.costHigh),
295:   }

302: export interface PricingAnalysisOutput {
303:   analysis: PricingAnalysis
304:   flipPlan: FlipPlan
