/**
 * Currency intelligence for worldwide marketplace support.
 *
 * PURE module — zero imports (client-safe AND importable by the scanner
 * mini-service via relative path, same rule as world-cities.ts / plans.ts).
 *
 * Facebook Marketplace prices every listing in the local currency of the
 * market it was posted in ($ in the US, £ in the UK, CA$ in Canada…). The
 * SSR/GraphQL payloads sometimes carry a proper ISO code in
 * listing_price.currency, but often only the formatted price text survives
 * the search-page payload ("£1,900", "CA$27,493", "NZ$3,800"). This module
 * resolves a trustworthy ISO-4217 code from whichever signals a listing
 * carries, so every layer downstream (comps, fair-value maths, alerts, UI)
 * can scope itself to ONE market instead of mixing dollars with pounds.
 */

/** ISO-4217 codes the app understands (validation set for FB-provided codes) */
export const KNOWN_CURRENCIES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  'AUD', 'USD', 'CAD', 'NZD', 'GBP', 'EUR', 'JPY', 'KRW', 'SGD', 'HKD', 'TWD',
  'MYR', 'IDR', 'THB', 'VND', 'PHP', 'INR', 'PKR', 'BDT', 'LKR', 'NPR', 'AED',
  'SAR', 'QAR', 'KWD', 'ILS', 'TRY', 'JOD', 'ZAR', 'NGN', 'KES', 'GHS', 'EGP',
  'MAD', 'ETB', 'TZS', 'MXN', 'BRL', 'ARS', 'CLP', 'COP', 'PEN', 'UYU', 'VES',
  'CRC', 'DOP', 'GTQ', 'SEK', 'NOK', 'DKK', 'CHF', 'PLN', 'CZK', 'HUF', 'ISK',
])

/** Validate an FB-provided currency string as a known ISO code */
export function normalizeCurrencyCode(raw: string | null | undefined): string | null {
  if (!raw) return null
  const up = raw.trim().toUpperCase()
  return KNOWN_CURRENCIES.has(up) ? up : null
}

/**
 * Detect the currency from formatted price text. Ordered by specificity —
 * prefixed/suffixed symbols before the bare "$" catch-all (a plain $ in a
 * non-AU market is USD; AU listings say $ too, so the watchlist context /
 * country fallback disambiguates those).
 */
export function detectCurrencyFromText(text: string | null | undefined): string | null {
  if (!text) return null
  const t = text.replace(/\s/g, '')
  if (/AU\$/.test(t)) return 'AUD'
  // Intl's compact AUD format ("A$45,000" — e.g. craigslist's JSON-LD display)
  // has no "U", so the FB-style pattern above misses it; a leading A$ is AUD
  // in every market that uses it.
  if (/^A\$/.test(t)) return 'AUD'
  if (/CA\$/.test(t)) return 'CAD'
  // eBay Canada's display strips the A: "C $8,430.60" — CA$ above misses it.
  if (/^C\$/.test(t)) return 'CAD'
  if (/NZ\$/.test(t)) return 'NZD'
  if (/US\$/.test(t)) return 'USD'
  if (/HK\$/.test(t)) return 'HKD'
  if (/MX\$|MEX\$/.test(t)) return 'MXN'
  if (/S\$/.test(t)) return 'SGD'
  if (/R\$/.test(t)) return 'BRL'
  if (/NT\$/.test(t)) return 'TWD'
  if (/£/.test(t)) return 'GBP'
  // eBay's European sites write EUR as text, not €: "EUR 81,60",
  // "143,04 EUR con cupón", "+EUR 9,86 verzendkosten".
  if (/EUR/i.test(t)) return 'EUR'
  if (/€/.test(t)) return 'EUR'
  if (/¥/.test(t)) return 'JPY'
  if (/₩/.test(t)) return 'KRW'
  if (/₱/.test(t)) return 'PHP'
  if (/₹/.test(t)) return 'INR'
  if (/₺/.test(t)) return 'TRY'
  if (/zł/i.test(t)) return 'PLN'
  if (/Kč/i.test(t)) return 'CZK'
  if (/Ft/i.test(t)) return 'HUF'
  if (/kr\.?$/i.test(t) || /kr$/i.test(t)) return 'SEK'
  if (/CHF/i.test(t)) return 'CHF'
  if (/R\s?\d/.test(t)) return 'ZAR'
  if (/\$/.test(t)) return 'USD'
  return null
}

## How the cap works

**Ranking happens before any write or detail fetch** (`src/lib/scan-ranking.ts`). Candidates are scored by:

1. **Discount vs same make + model live comps** — strongest signal
2. Fallback: same-make comps, then the AU baseline (weighted down)
3. Advertised price drop (strikethrough → current)
4. Title condition signals
5. Freshness

Junk is excluded before it can take a slot: placeholder `$1234` prices, parts/wrecks, and non-road vehicles. Ties are deterministic.

if (isVehicleVertical) {
    if (stored && storedFresh && (stored.fairValue != null || stored.flipEconomics != null)) {
      // FRESH STORED ANALYSIS — reuse it instead of re-running the pipeline.
      // The deal room then renders the exact numbers the card's score came
      // from; a live re-run can LOSE the valuation (sparse same-currency
      // comps, fleet cooldown, model scope) and show "Not enough pricing
      // data" on a listing the feed happily scored an hour ago. The
      // negotiation flip plan isn't serialised with the analysis, so rebuild
      // it from the stored valuation inputs.
      pricing = stored
      if (stored.fairValue != null && listing.price != null) {
        try {
          const { buildFlipPlan } = await import('@/lib/flip')
          flipPlan = buildFlipPlan({
            price: listing.price,
            title: listing.title,
            description: listing.description,
            condition: listing.condition,
            odometer: listing.odometer,
            year: listing.year,
            make: listing.make,
            model: listing.model,
            sellerType: listing.sellerType,
            postedAt: listing.postedAt,
            firstSeenAt: listing.firstSeenAt,
            previousPrice: listing.previousPrice,
            estimatedValue: stored.fairValue,
            valueLow: stored.fairValueLow,
            valueHigh: stored.fairValueHigh,
            marketMedian: stored.compValuation?.baseMedian ?? listing.marketMedian,
            transmission: listing.transmission ?? null,
            fuelType: listing.fuelType ?? null,
            currency: listing.currency,
          })
        } catch {
          flipPlan = null
        }
      }
    } else {
      const analyzed = await analyzePricing(db, {
        id: listing.id,
        title: listing.title,
        price: listing.price,
        // worldwide: the live rebuild must price in the listing's own currency
        // (offer scripts, verdict lines and recon values all format with it)
        currency: listing.currency,
        year: listing.year,
        make: listing.make,
        model: listing.model,
        description: listing.description,
        condition: listing.condition,
        odometer: listing.odometer,
        transmission: listing.transmission,
        fuelType: listing.fuelType,
        bodyStyle: listing.bodyStyle,
        sellerType: listing.sellerType,
        state: listing.state,
        titleStatus: listing.titleStatus,
        postedAt: listing.postedAt,
        firstSeenAt: listing.firstSeenAt,
        previousPrice: listing.previousPrice,
      })
      pricing = analyzed.analysis
      flipPlan = analyzed.flipPlan
      valuation = analyzed.valuation
      // GAP MERGE — when the live pass can't value the car (no comps, no
      // model), fill the holes from the stored analysis so the page never
      // downgrades a scored listing to "Not enough pricing data".
      if (stored) {
        pricing.fairValue = pricing.fairValue ?? stored.fairValue ?? null
        pricing.fairValueLow = pricing.fairValueLow ?? stored.fairValueLow ?? null
        pricing.fairValueHigh = pricing.fairValueHigh ?? stored.fairValueHigh ?? null
        pricing.compValuation = pricing.compValuation ?? stored.compValuation ?? null
        pricing.soldValuation = pricing.soldValuation ?? stored.soldValuation ?? null
        pricing.confidence = pricing.confidence ?? stored.confidence ?? null
        pricing.valuationSource = pricing.valuationSource ?? stored.valuationSource ?? null
        pricing.valuationFactors = pricing.valuationFactors ?? stored.valuationFactors ?? null
        pricing.valuationSources = pricing.valuationSources ?? stored.valuationSources ?? null
        pricing.verdictLine = pricing.verdictLine ?? stored.verdictLine ?? null
        pricing.valueVerdict = pricing.valueVerdict ?? stored.valueVerdict ?? null
        pricing.discountPct = pricing.discountPct ?? stored.discountPct ?? null
        pricing.modelAvailable = pricing.modelAvailable || stored.modelAvailable
        if ((pricing.comparables?.length ?? 0) === 0) pricing.comparables = stored.comparables
        if ((pricing.comparableStats?.count ?? 0) === 0) pricing.comparableStats = stored.comparableStats
        if ((pricing.reasonsUnderpriced?.length ?? 0) === 0) pricing.reasonsUnderpriced = stored.reasonsUnderpriced
        if (pricing.flipEconomics == null) pricing.flipEconomics = stored.flipEconomics ?? null
        pricing.profitable = pricing.profitable || stored.profitable
      }
    }
    valuation = valuation ?? (listing.valuationJson ? safeParseValuation(listing.valuationJson) : null)
  } else {
    pricing = stored
      ? stored
      : {
          analyzedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
          modelAvailable: false,
          modelFairValue: null,
          modelErrorBandPct: null,
          compValuation: null,
          comparables: [],
          comparableStats: {
            count: listing.compCount ?? 0,
            median: listing.marketMedian,
            low25: listing.marketLow,
            high75: listing.marketHigh,
            min: listing.marketLow,
            max: listing.marketHigh,
            avgOdometer: null,
            avgYear: null,
          },
          fairValue: listing.estimatedValue ?? listing.marketMedian,
          fairValueLow: listing.valueLow ?? listing.marketLow,
          fairValueHigh: listing.valueHigh ?? listing.marketHigh,
          confidence: (listing.valuationConfidence as 'high' | 'medium' | 'low') ?? 'low',
          valueVerdict: null,
          discountPct: listing.savingsPct != null ? -listing.savingsPct : null,

          verdictLine: null,
        }

      vin: listing.vin,
      vinDecoded: listing.vinDecoded,
      odometer: listing.odometer,
      transmission: listing.transmission,
      fuelType: listing.fuelType,
      exteriorColor: listing.exteriorColor,
      interiorColor: listing.interiorColor,
      drivetrain: listing.drivetrain,
      titleStatus: listing.titleStatus,
      numberOfOwners: listing.numberOfOwners,
      carfaxUrl: listing.carfaxUrl,
      dealershipName: listing.dealershipName,
      engineInfo: listing.engineInfo,
      specifications: specs,
      sellerName: listing.sellerName,
      sellerType: listing.sellerType,
      dealRating: listing.dealRating,
      isScam: listing.isScam,
      scamFlags: listing.scamFlags ? JSON.parse(listing.scamFlags) : [],
      marketAvg: listing.marketAvg,
      marketMedian: listing.marketMedian,
      marketLow: listing.marketLow,
      marketHigh: listing.marketHigh,
      compCount: listing.compCount,
      potentialProfit: listing.potentialProfit,
      roiPct: listing.roiPct,
      savingsPct: listing.savingsPct,
      estimatedValue: pricing.fairValue ?? listing.estimatedValue,
      valueLow: pricing.fairValueLow ?? listing.valueLow,
      valueHigh: pricing.fairValueHigh ?? listing.valueHigh,
      valuationConfidence: pricing.confidence ?? listing.valuationConfidence,
      valuation: valuation ?? (listing.valuationJson ? JSON.parse(listing.valuationJson) : null),
      scoredAt: listing.scoredAt,
      status: personal?.status ?? 'new',
      stale: listing.status === 'stale',
      watchlists: listing.watchlists
        .filter((wl) => wl.watchlist.userId === me)
        .map((wl) => ({
          id: wl.watchlistId,
          name: wl.watchlist.name,
          isNew: wl.isNew,
        })),
      // Per-marketplace source link — non-FB rows carry their stored URL
      // (their prefixed ids must not ride the Facebook URL builder)
      fbUrl: (listing.marketplace ?? 'FacebookMarketplace') !== 'FacebookMarketplace'
        ? (listing.listingUrl ?? null)
        : `https://www.facebook.com/marketplace/item/${listing.fbListingId}/`,
    },
    // full 6-step analysis: fair value, confidence, comparables (ranked),
    // reasons underpriced, repair breakdown, margin waterfall
    pricing,
    // compatibility: top comparable set in the old shape
    comps: pricing.comparables.map((c) => ({
      id: c.id,
      title: c.title,
      price: c.price,
      year: c.year,

      postedAt: c.postedAt,
      similarity: c.similarity,
      matchNotes: c.matchNotes,
      transmission: c.transmission,
      city: c.city,
    })),
    flipPlan,
  })
}

/**
 * Per-listing deal analysis — the spine of the pricing-intelligence pipeline.
 *
 * Runs the full six-step flow for one listing and produces everything the
 * ranking layer and the deal room need:
 *
 *   1. collect            — the listing row itself (scanned live from FB AU)
 *   2. comparables        — generation / variant / transmission / mileage /
 *                           local-market matched comp set + price stats
 *   3. fair market value  — gradient-boosted model prediction blended with
 *                           the live-comp valuation, with an honest
 *                           confidence grade and value band
 *   4. condition/repairs  — evidence-locked recon estimate from the ad's own
 *                           words (mechanical / cosmetic / tyres / service /
 *                           inspection), via the flip-plan step engine
 *   5. flip potential     — expected resale − purchase target − repairs −
 *                           transaction costs − contingency allowance
 *   6. ranking facts      — net margin, confidence, comparable listings and
 *                           the concrete reasons the car may be underpriced
 *
 * The key distinction, encoded structurally: a car priced below market value
 * is NOT automatically profitable to flip — `valueVerdict` (price vs fair
 * value) is kept separate from `profitable` (margin after repairs, costs and
 * contingency). The rating gate in scoring.ts only lets margin-positive
 * listings through as good-ROI deals.
 */

import type { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client'
import { estimateValue, type ValuationResult } from '../valuation'
import { buildFlipPlan, type FlipPlan, type FlipStep } from '../flip'
import { parseVehicleTitle } from '../vehicle'
import { findComparables, type ComparableListing, type ComparableStats } from './comparables'
import { predictListing } from './train'
import { loadPricingModel } from './model-store'
import { estimateFromSaleComps } from './sale-comps'
import { currencyFloor, formatMoneyCurrency } from '../currency'

export type ValueVerdict = 'underpriced' | 'fairly_priced' | 'overpriced'
export type ConfidenceGrade = 'high' | 'medium' | 'low'
export type RepairCategory =
  | 'inspection'
  | 'mechanical'
  | 'cosmetic'
  | 'tyres'
  | 'service'
  | 'rego'
  | 'selling'

export interface RepairItem {
  id: string
  title: string
  category: RepairCategory
  costLow: number
  costMid: number
  costHigh: number
  /** the ad's own words that triggered this repair item */
  evidence: string[]
}

export interface FlipEconomics {
  expectedResale: number
  /** which evidence produced expectedResale: durable sold comps or the
   *  asking-price haircut fallback */
  expectedResaleBasis?: 'sold-comps' | 'asking-gap'
  purchaseTarget: number
  repairs: number
  transactionCosts: number
  contingency: number
  netMargin: number
  netMarginLow: number
  netMarginHigh: number
  marginRoiPct: number
}

export interface PricingAnalysis {
  analyzedAt: string
  modelAvailable: boolean
  modelFairValue: number | null
  modelErrorBandPct: number | null
  compValuation: {
    estimatedValue: number | null
    baseMedian: number | null
    compCount: number
    confidence: ConfidenceGrade | null
    method: string | null
  } | null
  comparables: ComparableListing[]
  comparableStats: ComparableStats
  /** durable sold evidence — cars that actually left the market under our
   *  watch (or were imported from real sales). `estimatedValue` is the
   *  expected SALE price adjusted to this exact car; `askingEquivalent` is
   *  the same evidence expressed on the asking-price basis of fairValue. */
  soldValuation?: {
    estimatedValue: number | null
    askingEquivalent: number | null
    low: number | null
    high: number | null
    compCount: number
    exactCount: number
    widerCount: number
    confidence: ConfidenceGrade
    method: string
    medianSoldPrice: number | null
    medianDaysToSell: number | null
    askingGapPct: number | null
    bandPct: number | null
    sample: Array<{
      title: string
      price: number
      daysOnMarket: number | null
      year: number | null
      odometer: number | null
      observedAt: string
      basis: string
    }>
  } | null
  fairValue: number | null
  fairValueLow: number | null
  fairValueHigh: number | null
  confidence: ConfidenceGrade
  valueVerdict: ValueVerdict | null
  discountPct: number | null
  reasonsUnderpriced: string[]
  repairEstimate: {
    items: RepairItem[]
    totalLow: number
    totalMid: number
    totalHigh: number
  }
  flipEconomics: FlipEconomics | null
  profitable: boolean
  verdictLine: string | null
  /** Set when the value basis was clamped by the grade-gap cap (scoring.ts):
   *  comp evidence priced a higher grade of the item than the one listed. */
  valueVerdictNote?: string | null
  /** Which evidence tier produced the fair value (lib/estimate/types.ts):
   *  'live-comps' | 'web-evidence' | 'market-knowledge' | 'category-typical' */
  valuationSource?: string | null
  /** The human-readable factors behind the valuation (condition, brand tier,
   *  completeness…) — the deal room renders these as the "why" */
  valuationFactors?: Array<{ label: string; detail: string; impactPct?: number }> | null
  /** Web price references behind a web-evidence valuation */
  valuationSources?: Array<{ title: string; url: string; price: number; host: string }> | null
}

export interface AnalyzableListing {
  id: string
  title: string
  price: number | null
  /** marketplace currency (worldwide) — the ML model is AUD-trained and only
   *  fires on AUD listings; every other market runs on live same-currency
   *  comps, which stay honest in any currency */
  currency?: string | null
  year: number | null
  make: string | null
  model: string | null
  description: string | null
  condition: string | null
  odometer: number | null
  transmission: string | null
  fuelType?: string | null
  bodyStyle?: string | null
  sellerType: string | null
  state: string | null
  titleStatus: string | null
  postedAt: Date | null
  firstSeenAt: Date | null
  previousPrice: number | null
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Transaction costs + contingency (flip underwriting — market-agnostic)
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** Asking→realized haircut for a flipped car: fair value is a median of ASKING
 *  prices, private sales transact below asking, and a flipper sells at a small
 *  discount for speed. Mirrors the generic path's 12% haircut. */
export const CAR_REALIZED_SALE_PCT = 0.92

/** listing sundries (ads, detailing supplies, transfer/registration papers)
 * plus the estimated transfer/registration bite on purchase — scales with
 * price in the listing's own currency (a sane estimate in every market:
 * ~3% transfer-ish cost capped, plus a small fixed sundry block) */
export function transactionCosts(purchase: number): number {
  const transfer = Math.min(600, Math.max(150, Math.round(purchase * 0.03)))
  return 120 + transfer
}

/** contingency allowance — the unplanned (a PPI surprise, a gearbox flush,
 * a blown tyre on the test drive). 5% of purchase, floored at $250. */
export function contingencyAllowance(purchase: number): number {
  return Math.max(250, Math.round(purchase * 0.05))
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Fair-value blend
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function round50(n: number): number {
  return Math.max(0, Math.round(n / 50) * 50)
}

/** Keep negative margins negative; the market-value helper above is floored. */
function round50Signed(n: number): number {
  return Math.round(n / 50) * 50
}

function clamp(v: number, min: number, max: number): number {
  return Math.min(max, Math.max(min, v))
}

/**
 * Professional vehicle valuation engine.
 *
 * Estimates the current market value of a vehicle from LIVE marketplace
 * comparables — the real listings this app has scanned from Facebook
 * Marketplace — with adjustments for:
 *
 *   - kilometres (odometer): data-driven price-per-km slope across comps,
 *     falling back to an industry rule-of-thumb rate
 *   - model year: depreciation per year within the comp window
 *   - condition & description signals: service history, damage keywords,
 *     presentation, usage rate (km/year), listing condition field
 *   - listing recency: fresher comps weigh more (current market data)
 *   - seller mix: dealer vs private comps reported
 *
 * Methods, best available first:
 *   1. weighted multi-variable OLS regression (price ~ odometer + year)
 *   2. odometer/year-normalized weighted comps (hedonic adjustment)
 *   3. plain weighted median (insufficient data)
 */

import type { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client'
import { getCompPool, filterComps, titleTokens } from './comps'
import { currencyFloor } from './currency'

export interface ValuationInput {
  id: string
  title: string
  price: number | null
  year: number | null
  make: string | null
  model: string | null
  /** marketplace currency — comps are same-currency only (worldwide) */
  currency?: string | null
  odometer: number | null
  description: string | null
  condition?: string | null
  titleStatus?: string | null
  postedAt?: Date | null
}

export interface ConditionSignal {
  label: string
  impact: number // fraction of value, e.g. +0.14
  /** the ad's own words that matched — quoted in the UI and by the flip engine */
  evidence?: string
}

export interface ValuationAdjustment {
  label: string
  detail: string
  amount: number // dollars, applied on top of the base
}

export type ValuationMethod = 'regression' | 'weighted-comps' | 'median'

export interface ValuationResult {
  method: ValuationMethod
  confidence: 'high' | 'medium' | 'low'
  compCount: number
  compsWithOdometer: number
  dealerComps: number
  privateComps: number
  // raw (unadjusted) comp stats
  baseMedian: number
  rawAvg: number
  rawLow: number
  rawHigh: number
  // model details
  odometerRatePerKm: number // $ per km used for the odometer adjustment
  yearRatePct: number // fraction of median per model year
  subjectOdometer: number | null
  compsAvgOdometer: number | null
  subjectYear: number | null
  compsAvgYear: number | null
  // output
  baseEstimate: number // market-normalized value before condition modifier
  conditionModifierPct: number // e.g. +0.04
  estimatedValue: number
  low: number
  high: number
  conditionScore: number // -1..1
  conditionSignals: ConditionSignal[]
  adjustments: ValuationAdjustment[]
}

const YEAR_WINDOW = 3
const YEAR_RATE = 0.025 // 2.5% of median per model year
const FALLBACK_KM_RATE = 2.2e-6 // fraction of median per km (~2.2% per 10,000 km)
const KM_RATE_MIN = 8e-7 // sanity bounds for a data-driven slope
const KM_RATE_MAX = 4e-6
const CONDITION_WEIGHT = 0.08 // full score ±1 → ±8% of value
const REGRESSION_MIN_COMPS = 6
const RECENCY_HALF_DAYS = 45 // weight 1.0 now → decays with listing age

function clamp(v: number, min: number, max: number): number {
  return Math.min(max, Math.max(min, v))
}

function median(values: number[]): number | null {
  if (values.length === 0) return null
  const sorted = [...values].sort((a, b) => a - b)
  const mid = Math.floor(sorted.length / 2)
  return sorted.length % 2 === 0 ? (sorted[mid - 1] + sorted[mid]) / 2 : sorted[mid]
}

/** Weighted median: accumulate weights until half the total is crossed */
function weightedMedian(entries: Array<{ value: number; weight: number }>): number | null {
  if (entries.length === 0) return null
  const sorted = [...entries].sort((a, b) => a.value - b.value)
  const total = sorted.reduce((s, e) => s + e.weight, 0)
  let acc = 0
  for (const e of sorted) {
    acc += e.weight
    if (acc >= total / 2) return e.value
  }
  return sorted[sorted.length - 1].value
}

/** Recency weight — current market data counts more than stale listings */

So the valuation stack is reasonably strong. The missing piece is sold data, which now works after restart. But the user asks to "build up a strong estimation". We can:
- Run backfill/rescore all active listings so every listing has a current valuation and the new sold path.
- Ensure the scanner's sold evidence writes work.
- Add a "valuation health" check script / data quality guard.
- Maybe improve the model training corpus: retrain with all listings and new sold observations? With 0 sold, no.

Could add a **sold-evidence bootstrap** from hidden listings that have been off-market? No stale. Hidden rows are likely junk; not sales.

Could add **listing age-based sale inference for hidden rows**? Hidden statuses might include user-hidden cars that are still on market, so no.

Maybe we can query the Facebook marketplace for "sold" listings? Facebook search has `availability=sold`? In Marketplace, sold listings may still be accessible via item ID but not search. No.

Could import from a public dataset? Maybe there's an Australian used car sales dataset online. But user data should be local. We could add support for a CSV (already exists). We could create a small seed of *actual* recent sold prices from public sources? Fabricating or scraping could be questionable. We shouldn't invent data.

Let's focus on making the estimator more robust with **cross-source comparisons** and **uncertainty calibration**:
1. **Comp-quality weighting**: `estimateValue` weights comps by recency and trim overlap, but not by distance/local market, seller type, or odometer. It adjusts odometer/year but doesn't weight comps by proximity. Could improve.
2. **Outlier handling**: weighted median robust.
3. **Condition adjustment**: `estimateValue` applies condition modifier based on subject description; comps' condition isn't adjusted (comp condition unknown). Fine.
4. **Confidence**: currently `high` requires model + compCount>=6 + valuation high. Fine.
5. **Blend**: model weight may be too high for thin comps. But model MAPE 49%. With 3-5 comps, wComp = 0.21-0.36, so model 64-79% — too much model! That's a weakness. For 3 comps, the model dominates despite comps being direct evidence. The comment says "comps get up to 65% weight as the sample grows; the model carries the rest". But with 3 comps, 21% comps, 79% model. Given the model's 49% MAPE, direct comps should dominate even at 3. We could change to a stronger comp weight:
   - wComp = min(0.8, 0.35 + compCount * 0.07) → 3 comps: 0.56; 6: 0.77; 10: 0.8.
   - Or use sold weight and comp count together.
   This would make estimates more grounded in actual local listings. But if comps are noisy, model smooths. A 50/50 at 3 comps is reasonable.
   
   Current `compFair` uses `valuation.estimatedValue` only if confidence !== low; else baseMedian. For 3 comps, confidence is low? In `estimateValue`, confidence rules at the end. Let's check.

With 3 comps, confidence low, so `compFair = valuation.baseMedian` (raw median, not adjusted for km/year/condition). Then blend with model 21% comps / 79% model. That is indeed weak: the adjusted comp estimate is discarded for <4 comps. We should use `valuation.estimatedValue` regardless of confidence, perhaps with a discount for low confidence, rather than raw median. The adjustment for year/km/condition is valuable even with 3 comps. Why did they use baseMedian when low? Possibly to avoid overfitting adjustments on small samples. But using raw median ignores year/km differences. Could blend baseMedian and estimatedValue for low confidence:
```ts
const compFair = valuation
  ? valuation.confidence !== 'low'
    ? valuation.estimatedValue
    : Math.round(0.5 * valuation.estimatedValue + 0.5 * valuation.baseMedian)
  : null
```
And increase comp weight at 3 comps:
```ts
const wComp = Math.min(0.75, 0.3 + compCount * 0.06) // 3:0.48, 5:0.6, 8:0.75
```
This makes direct local evidence more influential. But we must ensure ratings don't become overconfident. `rateWithMargin` caps at good when compCount<3; at 3-5 it can be excellent if profitable, which is fine. Confidence remains low/medium.

Is this "stronger"? Yes: less reliance on a 49% MAPE model. But could worsen if comps are noisy. Weighted median is robust; using 48% comp weight at 3 comps seems reasonable. Current 21% is too low.

Also for `compFair` when `valuation` is null, model only. Fine.

Another improvement: **use sold evidence to calibrate the live comp asking prices**. We have `askingGapPct` measured from sold observations. If sold evidence exists, we could adjust comp fair value downward? But fairValue is asking-equivalent, so no; expectedResale already uses sold.

Another: **model error band** is 30%, and low confidence band = 37.5%. Fine.

Another: **condition adjustment** only ±8%; maybe too narrow but okay.

Another: **year rate** 2.5%/yr is low for old cars; data-driven regression handles it when enough comps. For 3 comps, fallback 2.5% may be too low. But not critical.

Maybe the best "strong estimation" improvement is **retraining the model with a larger corpus and better labels**. We now have 710 listings, but model trained on 889 (maybe from a bigger corpus before cleanup). Retraining may not help. Could include hidden rows? They are valid market prices, just not shown. messages.summary:
## Objective
- Improve Dealify’s valuation accuracy using sold evidence and broader comparisons, cap each scan at the 5 best new listings, and fix listing clicks so the deal room loads and can reach the original marketplace listing.

## Requirements
- User: “build a better valuation system. use previous sale data and other comparisons to make a more accurate pricing system.”
- User: “add a limiter per scan, so that it can only pull 5 listings per scan. if it goes over, choose the 5 best options.”
- User: “just build up a strong estimation for pricing valuation. also when i click on a listing, it doesnt load so that i can go to the actual listing.”
- Preserve Dealify design language, onboarding/signup behavior, and existing pricing architecture.
- Keep “Start free trial” routed to onboarding (`/personalise?start=1`), not sign-in/create-account.

## Decisions
- Sold evidence is the strongest valuation input; blend it with live asking comps and the ML model, adjusting for year, odometer, condition, transmission, state, and recency.
- Durable `SaleObservation` store: stale-sweep listings become inferred sales; CSV imports can carry actual transaction prices.
- Fair value remains asking-price-equivalent; sold estimates convert via `askingEquivalent`.
- Per-scan cap applies to **new** listings only; existing price updates, restores, and backfill enrichment are unaffected.
- Ranking happens before any DB write/detail fetch: discount vs same make+model comps (1) → same-make comps (0.45) → AU baseline (0.3), plus price-drop, condition, freshness; junk dropped.
- `enrichBatchLimit` stays 3; `scoreBatchLimit` default 6.
- Live comps should outweigh the ~49%-MAPE model at small samples; adaptive year window and weighted mean for 1–2 comps.
- Detail view must fail gracefully and always expose the original listing URL carried from the feed card.

## Work State

### Completed
- Full sold-evidence valuation system: `SaleObservation` model, `sale-comps.ts`, `analyze.ts` blend, `market-intel.ts` sold-first ladder, stale-sweep capture, CSV import/backfill, deal-room sold panel, feed “Sold est.” labels; worklog Task 71.
- Per-scan limiter: `scan-ranking.ts`, `maxNewListingsPerScan` default 5, pre-write selection, `skippedNew`, best-first ingest order, scanner-service log; worklog Task 72.
- Root-caused detail 500: running processes held the old Prisma client, so `db.saleObservation` was `undefined`; error was `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'count')` at `sale-comps.ts:365`.
- Added `saleObservationDelegate` guards so a stale/missing client degrades to “no sold evidence” instead of 500ing valuations.
- Restarted Next dev on port 3001 and the scanner service once; detail API then returned 200 in ~1.2s.
- Added `selectedListingUrl` to the app store, feed passes `l.fbUrl`, and `listing-detail.tsx` now has an error state with Retry and “Open original listing”.
- Strengthened valuation: adjusted comp value blended 60/40 with raw median on low confidence; comp weight `min(0.75, 0.3 + count*0.06)` for 3+ comps, 0.45 for 2, 0.3 for 1.
- Added adaptive ±6-year comp widening when tight ±3-year comps are thin, with confidence kept low when widened.
- Switched 1–2 comp estimates to weighted mean; 3+ keep weighted median.
- Fixed `persistScore` so `estimatedValue` prefers blended `pricing.fairValue` over comp-only `valuation.estimatedValue`.
- Fixed model parsing for ad-copy separators (`2011 Nissan Murano | Automatic | V6 | Spacious…` → `Murano`) and added model-tail repair in scoring.
- Rescored 326 active vehicles with the latest code: all priced, 0 errors.
- Evaluated retraining on the current corpus (R² 0.055, MAPE 43.5%, predictions ~$3.5k) and restored the previous model (`trainedAt 2026-10-26`, `rowCount 889`, R² 0.6107, MAPE 48.77%).

### Active
- Final validation/cleanup after the valuation and detail fixes.
- Two sub-floor rows remain inconsistent: `2008 Toyota Yaris` (price 400, `estimatedValue` 4388 vs `pricingJson.fairValue` 4250) and `2014 Toyota Prius` (price 500, 5625 vs 4600).
- Scanner service is currently stopped after being killed for the single-writer rescore.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Restart the scanner supervisor (`nohup bun mini-services/scanner-service/supervisor.ts >> .zscripts/scanner-3003.log 2>&1 &`) and verify `http://127.0.0.1:3003/health`.
2. Delete temporary scripts: `scripts/_tmp-check-analyze.ts`, `_tmp-check-detail.ts`, `_tmp-sample-valuation.ts`, `_tmp-near-comps.ts`, `_tmp-debug-murano.ts`, `_tmp-rescore-one.ts`, `_tmp-rescore-vehicles.ts`.
3. Run `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bunx eslint src scripts mini-services --ext .ts,.tsx`, `bun scripts/check-sale-comps.ts`, `bun scripts/check-valuation-integration.ts`, and `bun scripts/check-scan-ranking.ts`.
4. Retest a vehicle detail request and the feed API; confirm 200 responses and consistent `estimatedValue` / `pricingJson.fairValue`.
5. Decide whether to hide the two sub-floor Yaris/Prius rows or leave them out of valuation.
6. Add worklog Task 73 covering the stale-client crash, detail error UI/source link, parser fixes, adaptive comp window, blend/consistency changes, and rescore.

## Relevant Files
- `src/lib/pricing/sale-comps.ts`: sold estimator, cache, write/remove guards for missing Prisma delegate.
- `src/lib/pricing/analyze.ts`: fair-value blend, sold weighting, comp-vs-model weights.
- `src/lib/valuation.ts`: live comp estimator, adaptive year window, 1–2 comp weighted mean.

1136:## Task 71 — Better valuation system: durable sold evidence + adjusted sold comps (2026-11-12)
1137-
1138-- USER REQUEST: "build a better valuation system. use previous sale data and other comparisons to make a more accurate pricing system."
1139-- WHAT SHIPPED:
1140-  1. `SaleObservation` model (prisma) — durable sale records that survive listing deletion: make/model/year/trim/body/odometer/condition score/transmission/state, final asking, transaction (or gap-adjusted) sold price, `priceBasis` (`actual` | `asking-gap` | `price-drop`), price-drop %, days-on-market, observedAt, confidence, evidence JSON. Unique `listingId` (relist updates one row) + unique `(source, externalId)` for idempotent imports.
1141-  2. `src/lib/pricing/sale-comps.ts` — the sold-comparable engine: cached sold pool (60s TTL + cross-process row-count invalidation), hierarchical matching (exact family → same make+body → same body other make), Theil–Sen year/odometer rate fits with clamped fallbacks, condition/transmission/state adjustments, recency half-life, outlier clip, robust weighted median+mean, Kish effective sample size, IQR band, honest high/medium/low confidence, factors + top samples. Returns both the expected SALE value and its `askingEquivalent` (so fairValue semantics don't change).
1142-  3. `analyze.ts` — sold evidence is blended into fairValue (soldWeight up to 0.85 when there are no live comps, 0.7 with live comps), narrows the value band, powers `expectedResale` (`expectedResaleBasis: 'sold-comps' | 'asking-gap'`), adds a "sold evidence" underpriced reason, and exposes `soldValuation` + `valuationSource: 'sold-comps'` + sold-aware `valuationFactors`.
1143-  4. `market-intel.ts` — the evidence ladder now reads `SaleObservation` first (stale-listing fallback retained for pre-observation DBs); sold rows carry adjusted sale value, median sold price, measured asking→sale gap, liquidity days and sold-backed resale.
1144-  5. Capture paths: maintenance stale sweep writes a sale observation for every listing that leaves the market (batch 500) and reports `recordedSales`; scanner restores re-seen stale listings and deletes their inferred sale rows; detail-route photo refresh un-stales + removes the observation.   if (!make) return false

/** Flip verticals — the "flip anything" taxonomy.
 *
 *  FlipRadar (born Dealify) started as a car-only deal sniper. It now covers every flip
 *  vertical: the scanner classifies each incoming listing into one of these
 *  verticals, watchlists are created per vertical, comping + flip economics
 *  adapt per vertical, and the UI (onboarding quiz, feed chips, watchlist
 *  editor, listing detail) renders vertical-aware controls.
 *
 *  CLIENT-SAFE: no zod / db / server-only imports — both the app components
 *  and the server libs (scanner, scoring, profile) import from here.
 */

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Types
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export type VerticalId =
  | 'vehicles'
  | 'electronics'
  | 'furniture'
  | 'fashion'
  | 'collectibles'
  | 'bikes'
  | 'gaming'
  | 'appliances'
  | 'tools'
  | 'other'

  id: VerticalId
  /** Full label for pickers and detail headers ("Cars & Vehicles"). */
  label: string

  short: string
  emoji: string
  blurb: string
  /** Marketplace search query used when a watchlist has no query of its own. */
  defaultQuery: string
  /** Classification keywords — matched on word boundaries against title +
  *  description. First match per keyword only (hits, not occurrences). */
  keywords: string[]
  /** Example flips for marketing surfaces (landing hero card, ticker, FAQ). */
  examples: string[]
}

/**

 *
 * Every valuation / market-stats / re-score call used to re-fetch up to 5,000
 * listing rows from SQLite and re-normalise them in JS — twice per scored
 * listing (valuation.ts + scoring.ts). This module loads the pool once and
 * keeps it warm:

 *     process, since both the Next.js server and the scanner mini-service
 *     share the same SQLite file)

/**
 * Distinctive title tokens for trim/spec matching — make/model words and

const GENERIC_TOKENS = new Set([

  'turbo', 'km', 'kms', 'klms', 'the', 'and', 'with', 'only', 'very', 'new',
  'sale', 'sell', 'selling', 'sold', 'price', 'offer', 'ono', 'negotiable',
  'urgent', 'must', 'great', 'good', 'excellent', 'condition', 'clean', 'tidy',
])

export function titleTokens(title: string, make?: string | null, model?: string | null): Set<string> {
  const drop = new Set<string>()
  for (const w of [make, model]) {
    for (const t of normalizeKey(w).split(' ')) if (t) drop.add(t)
  }
  const out = new Set<string>()
  for (const t of normalizeKey(title).split(' ')) {
    if (!t || t.length < 3) continue
    if (/^\d+$/.test(t)) continue // years, sizes, badge numbers
    if (drop.has(t) || GENERIC_TOKENS.has(t)) continue
    out.add(t)
  }
  return out
}

## Objective
- Improve Dealify’s pricing accuracy so valuation reflects condition and product-specific factors per vertical, while keeping the recently fixed deal-room flow and the profit-scale visual in good shape.

## Requirements
- User: “with the pricing, take into consideration, condition and various other factors depending on the actual product.”
- Earlier: “build a better valuation system. use previous sale data and other comparisons to make a more accurate pricing system.”
- Earlier: “add a limiter per scan, so that it can only pull 5 listings per scan. if it goes over, choose the 5 best options.”
- Earlier: “just build up a strong estimation for pricing valuation. also when i click on a listing, it doesnt load so that i can go to the actual listing.”
- Earlier: profit scale “green section is too short and the orange section is too long”; then “it should look similar to this” with a smooth red→orange→yellow→lime→green reference bar.
- Preserve Dealify design language, onboarding/signup behavior, and existing pricing architecture.
- Keep “Start free trial” routed to onboarding (`/personalise?start=1`), not sign-in/create-account.

## Decisions
- Sold evidence remains the strongest valuation input; blend with live comps and the ML model, adjusted for year, odometer, condition, transmission, state, and recency.
- Product-aware factor layer lives in `src/lib/estimate/item-factors.ts` so both generic scoring and the estimate engine share it.
- `valueMultiplier` deliberately excludes brand tier to avoid double-counting (brand is already embedded in same-brand comps; factor model applies brand separately).
- Generic comp valuation will condition-normalize each comp to a “good used” baseline, then apply the subject’s completeness/product extras.
- Vehicle condition weight should increase from 8% to 12% in both live-comps and sold-comps estimators.
- Profit scale now uses a smooth `PROFIT_STOPS` palette; marker colour is interpolated from the same stops so dot and track agree.

## Work State

### Completed
- Task 73 validation: scanner restarted and healthy; temporary scripts removed; `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bunx eslint src scripts mini-services --ext .ts,.tsx`, `check-sale-comps.ts`, `check-valuation-integration.ts`, `check-scan-ranking.ts` all pass.
- Rescored the two sub-floor rows (`2008 Toyota Yaris`, `2014 Toyota Prius`); `estimatedValue` vs `pricingJson.fairValue` mismatches now **0**.
- Added missing makes `Renault`, `Chrysler`, `Daewoo`, `Daihatsu` to `COMMON_MAKES`; rescored those four rows. Coverage is now **374/375** active vehicles priced (only `"Car for sell"` lacks an identifiable make).
- Authenticated feed and detail API both return **200**; detail ~1.4s with original listing URL present.
- Worklog Task 73 appended covering stale-Prisma crash, detail error UI/source link, parser fixes, adaptive comp window, blend/consistency changes, rescore, model-retrain rejection.
- Profit scale updated twice; final version uses smooth `PROFIT_STOPS` (`#c0392b → #d35400 → #e67e22 → #edb32c → #f1c40f → #c3d63b → #9bd142 → #6fc24a → #56b947`) and interpolated marker colour. Worklog Task 74 appended.
- Rewrote `src/lib/estimate/item-factors.ts` with severity-first condition detection, `detectConditionGrade` export, vertical-aware product rules, `productFactors`, `valueMultiplier`, and `partsGrade`.

### Active
- Product-aware pricing integration is partially done: only `item-factors.ts` has been rewritten; downstream consumers still need updating.
- `factor-model.ts` still multiplies condition/completeness separately and will double-count once `valueMultiplier` is wired in.
- Generic scoring still uses raw `stats.median`; condition-normalized comp adjustment not yet applied.
- Vehicle `CONDITION_WEIGHT` still `0.08` in `valuation.ts` and `sale-comps.ts`.
- New `item-factors.ts` has not yet been type-checked or linted after the rewrite.

### Blocked
- (none)

1. Update `src/lib/estimate/factor-model.ts` to use `opts.factors.valueMultiplier` plus brand tier, and append `opts.factors.productFactors` to the displayed factor list without re-applying condition/completeness.

3. Add `condition` to `CompRow` and `loadPool` in `src/lib/comps.ts`.
4. In `src/lib/scoring.ts` `scoreGenericListing`, compute subject `extractItemFactors`, condition-normalize comp prices with `detectConditionGrade` + `conditionMultiplier`, apply subject extras, and use the adjusted basis for `valueBasis`, `fairValueLow/High`, `compValuation.estimatedValue`, and `valuationFactors`.
5. Raise vehicle condition weight to `0.12` and clamp to ±`0.12` in `src/lib/valuation.ts`; raise `CONDITION_WEIGHT` to `0.12` in `src/lib/pricing/sale-comps.ts`.
6. Add `scripts/check-product-factors.ts` covering battery health, cracked screen, DS vs worn sneakers, controller bundles, bare tool vs kit, solid timber vs flat pack, replica/authenticity, and multiplier clamping.
7. Run `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bunx eslint`, and the check scripts; sample generic valuations; append worklog Task 75.
